Edit here, never in spec.md.

areas.drag: Pointer drag and drop: activation, capture, feedback, drop, cancel, scroll

areas.announce: What assistive technology is told, and when

rules.rule: A drag that must work with touch SHOULD be built on Pointer Events; native HTML drag and drop MAY be used only where files, other windows or other apps must be dragged in or out.
rules.why: Native drag and drop has weak touch support and a fixed preview; pointer events give one code path for mouse, pen and touch. Native DnD is the only way to cross the window.

rules.rule: A press MUST NOT become a drag until it passes an activation constraint: a mouse or pen moves a distance (about 4px); a finger rests a delay (about 250ms) without drifting past a tolerance (about 5px). Only one constraint applies per input type.
rules.why: Without it a click starts a drag, and on touch a swipe that meant to scroll grabs the item.

validated.where: a web-component kanban board, Chromium (Playwright)
validated.finding: A click, and a press moved 2px, stay clicks and move nothing; a touch that moves past 5px at once moves nothing (the page may scroll); a touch held 320ms then moved carries the card.
validated.check: browser test: mouse click, sub-threshold move, CDP touch swipe and rested touch; all fail against the build without pointer drag

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: an HTML table of 6 columns and 8 rows in a scroll box, with a sticky header row and a sticky first column, columns reordered by the header and rows by a handle; headless Chromium 159 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only
validated.finding: Holds unchanged for a table column reordered by its header and for a row reordered by a handle.
validated.check: "col: a 2px press is a click, not a drag" and "row: a 2px press is a click, not a drag" (control: no distance threshold; the click still sorts the column or opens the row menu) and "col: touch: a swipe from the header is not a drag", "row: touch: a swipe from the handle is not a drag" (control: touch uses the distance constraint, no delay).

validated.where: a list whose rows drag after a 250 ms hold, CDP touch under touch emulation in headless Chromium
validated.finding: A finger that moved within 240 ms of touching down was treated as a swipe and nothing was dragged; one that rested 260 ms or more dragged the row. With the hold set to 400 ms a 350 ms rest no longer dragged. A touch drag test therefore has to rest longer than the hold before its first move.
validated.check: send the moves at once: the drag must not start; remove the hold: it starts

rules.rule: touch-action MUST be set in CSS before a press begins, since a change during a press is ignored. When the whole item is draggable inside a scrolling page, the drag SHOULD leave touch-action alone, use the delay constraint, and cancel the scroll from a non-passive touchmove listener once the drag is live. When only a handle drags, touch-action: none goes on the handle only.
rules.why: touch-action: none on a whole item stops the page from scrolling when a finger starts on it; pointer listeners cannot cancel the browser's touch scroll, but a non-passive touchmove can.
rules.note: The delay path is validated (drag.activation); that the touchmove listener is what stops the scroll on a real device is not yet measured.

rules.rule: Once a drag is live the element SHOULD capture the pointer (setPointerCapture), and the drag MUST end on pointerup and cancel on pointercancel; the move, up and cancel listeners are removed when it ends.
rules.why: Without capture, moves stop when the pointer leaves the element; without a pointercancel path, an interrupted touch leaves the item lifted.

rules.rule: While dragging, the lifted item SHOULD follow the pointer by a transform (the CSS translate property composes with an existing transform) and keep its slot, so no other box moves until the drop.
rules.why: Reflowing the list under the pointer moves the targets the user is aiming at; the drop indicator, not the layout, says where the item lands.

validated.where: a web-component kanban board, Chromium (Playwright)
validated.finding: Every lane keeps its height mid-drag; the card returns to no translate and no lifted state after the drop.
validated.check: browser test compares lane heights before and during a drag

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: an HTML table of 6 columns and 8 rows in a scroll box, with a sticky header row and a sticky first column, columns reordered by the header and rows by a handle; headless Chromium 159 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only
validated.finding: Holds unchanged for a table column reordered by its header and for a row reordered by a handle.
validated.check: "col: nothing else moves while it is carried, and it keeps its slot" and "row: nothing else moves while it is carried, and it keeps its slot" (control: the DOM is reordered while carrying). The "item" is a set of cells (a header and one cell per row, or every cell of a row); translate is set on each cell. See proposed drag.table-cells-follow.

validated.where: a reorderable list and a board on a shared drag-preview helper, web components in shadow DOM, headless Chromium
validated.finding: The item can leave its slot for the top layer as a manual popover moved by translate while a placeholder of its measured size holds the slot: the list kept its height and the placeholder its row's height and place, and the card was drawn outside its scroll box. Being the item and not a clone, it kept its container's ::slotted styles; the popover's user-agent box and colour rules were pinned to the item's computed values first.
validated.check: "the ghost appears only past the threshold, in the top layer…" and "kanban: the card lifts into the top layer out of its scroll box…"; fail on the code before the change (negative control run). WebKit not run.

rules.note: Atlassian keeps the original at opacity 0.4 and drags a separate preview; moving the item itself is the simpler variant when the item's styles come from its container.

rules.rule: Where the item will land SHOULD be shown by a 2px line in the middle of the gap with a terminal mark at its start; a container with no items MUST show no line, and the container that would take the item SHOULD be tinted only when it is not the item's own.
rules.why: A line names a position between items; an empty list has no between, so the container itself is the answer.

validated.where: a web-component kanban board, Chromium (Playwright)
validated.finding: Exactly one line shows, in the lane under the pointer; an empty lane shows no line and is tinted.
validated.check: browser test reads each lane's line and tint mid-drag

rules.rule: Escape, pointercancel and the page becoming hidden MUST cancel a live drag, put the item back where it started, fire no change event, and say so.
rules.why: A drag the user cannot abandon is a trap; a cancel that fires a change makes the app persist a move nobody made.

validated.where: a web-component kanban board, Chromium (Playwright)
validated.finding: Escape mid-drag restores the order, fires no move event and announces the card put back.
validated.check: browser test, negative control against the build without pointer drag

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: an HTML table of 6 columns and 8 rows in a scroll box, with a sticky header row and a sticky first column, columns reordered by the header and rows by a handle; headless Chromium 159 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only
validated.finding: Holds unchanged for a table column reordered by its header and for a row reordered by a handle.
validated.check: "col: Escape puts it back and fires nothing" and "row: Escape puts it back and fires nothing" (control: no Escape listener), "col: touch: pointercancel puts it back and fires nothing" and "row: touch: pointercancel puts it back and fires nothing" (control: pointercancel treated as a drop), "col: a cancel is announced" and "row: a cancel is announced". validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: a sortable list of six rows in a page that scrolls, each dragged by a handle (mouse past 4px, finger after 250ms), with a keyboard mode on the handle and Move up and Move down buttons; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and page.keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only

validated.where: controls whose drag sets a value (a rotary choice, a number window, a scrubbed number with a letter handle, a two-axis colour plane) and a canvas node moved by drag, web components, headless Chromium with page.mouse and the keyboard
validated.finding: Escape with the button down put each back to the value before the press and fired no change event; the canvas node announced the cancel. The release that followed did nothing

rules.rule: The click that follows a drop MUST be swallowed (a capturing listener that stops it, removed on the next task or at the next pointerdown, whichever comes first), so a drop never also activates what is under the pointer.
rules.why: Browsers fire click after pointerup on the common ancestor; dropping onto a button or link would otherwise press it. Input is scheduled ahead of timers, so a press made just after the release can arrive before the next task; it starts a new gesture whose click must land.

validated.where: a web-component kanban board, Chromium (Playwright)
validated.finding: No click reaches the document after a drag and drop; a plain click still does.
validated.check: browser test counts capturing document clicks

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: an HTML table of 6 columns and 8 rows in a scroll box, with a sticky header row and a sticky first column, columns reordered by the header and rows by a handle; headless Chromium 159 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only
validated.finding: Holds unchanged for a table column reordered by its header and for a row reordered by a handle.
validated.check: "col: the click after a drop is swallowed" and "row: the click after a drop is swallowed" (control: no capturing click listener). Measured in both engines: the click only arrives when the drop leaves the pressed node in place (carried and dropped in its own slot); it then lands on the header's sort button or the row handle, which would sort the table or open the Move menu. A drop that re-inserted the pressed node produced no click at all, so that case has no control that bites.

validated.where: a value window that steps on a click in its upper or lower half and rolls on a drag, and a canvas whose ports are picked by a click and joined by a drag; web components, headless Chromium with page.mouse
validated.finding: After a drag, no click stepped the window and no port was picked; a plain click still did both
validated.check: "24px up is four programs, and the click after the drop is swallowed" and "the drop is no click: nothing picked"; fails on the code before the change (negative control run by the build session, not re-run here)

validated.where: a shared pointer-drag helper on Pointer Events, a reorderable list in shadow DOM, headless Chromium
validated.finding: With the swallow removed only by a zero timeout, a button clicked at once after the release got no click: the timer's removal ran after the next press and its click. With a capturing pointerdown listener that also removes the swallow, that click landed and the drop's own click was still swallowed.
validated.check: "a press made fast after a drop still clicks"; fails with the timer-only removal (negative control run). WebKit not run.

rules.rule: A drag SHOULD scroll the nearest scroll box that can still move, or the page, while the pointer is within an edge band (about 40px) of its side, every animation frame, and re-evaluate the target as it scrolls.
rules.why: With touch scrolling cancelled during a drag, an item cannot otherwise reach a place outside the visible part of a list.

validated.where: a web-component kanban board in a 160px overflow box, Chromium (Playwright)
validated.finding: Holding a dragged card 10px from the box's bottom edge for 400ms scrolls it by more than 20px.
validated.check: browser test reads scrollTop

rules.rule: A drag start MUST cancel the press's default action (preventDefault on pointerdown) and focus its own part explicitly; a draggable surface SHOULD also set user-select: none (with -webkit-user-select), and an item with other interactive parts SHOULD drag only from a handle.
rules.why: Otherwise the press starts a text selection that follows the drag across the page. WebKit keeps extending it even under pointer capture and user-select: none on the pressed element; only cancelling the press stops it, and cancelling also stops the default focus, so the code must focus.

validated.where: knobs, a range slider and other drag controls, WebKit and Chromium (Playwright)
validated.finding: Dragging a knob across page text selected it in WebKit but not in Chromium; user-select: none alone did not stop it in WebKit; preventDefault on pointerdown did, in both engines.
validated.check: browser test in both engines reads getSelection() after a drag; a plain element's drag is the positive control that does select

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: an HTML table of 6 columns and 8 rows in a scroll box, with a sticky header row and a sticky first column, columns reordered by the header and rows by a handle; headless Chromium 159 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only
validated.finding: Holds unchanged for a table column reordered by its header and for a row reordered by a handle.
validated.check: Column: "col: carrying across cells from the header's own surface selects no text" (control: no preventDefault and no user-select none; Chromium selected "Team", WebKit selected most of the table). Focus half, both axes: "col: the pressed part takes focus although the press's default is cancelled" and "row: the pressed part takes focus although the press's default is cancelled" (control: preventDefault kept, explicit focus removed). Row: the selection half is NOT proven: the handle is a button and a press on a button started no selection in either engine, so the control did not bite and the check was dropped.

rules.rule: A drop SHOULD update the UI at once (optimistically) and persist afterwards; it MAY flash the moved item briefly (Atlassian: about 700ms), and never under prefers-reduced-motion.
rules.why: Waiting for the server makes the item jump back and forth; the flash shows where it went.

rules.rule: A press that ends without becoming a drag (a click, a swipe) MUST leave no state behind that blocks the next press; a new press replaces any earlier one still being followed.
rules.why: A guard set at pointerdown and cleared only when a drag ends stays set after a plain click, so every later drag is ignored; tests that only drive drags that start never see it.

validated.where: a sortable list on Pointer Events in a React UI kit, vitest with happy-dom and a headless Chrome drag pass
validated.finding: After a click on the grip with no movement, the next press dragged nothing. The browser pass found it; the unit tests had not. Stopping any earlier press on pointerdown fixed it.
validated.check: unit test "a click on the grip, with no movement, is no drag" fails on the code before the fix (re-run at the fix's parent commit with the new test) and passes after; the test was extended with a drag after the click

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: an HTML table of 6 columns and 8 rows in a scroll box, with a sticky header row and a sticky first column, columns reordered by the header and rows by a handle; headless Chromium 159 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only
validated.finding: Holds unchanged for a table column reordered by its header and for a row reordered by a handle.
validated.check: "col: a click leaves nothing that hijacks the next press" and "row: a click leaves nothing that hijacks the next press" (control: a click leaves its pending press in place and a new press is ignored). Mouse only; a touch swipe followed by a touch drag was not tested.

rules.rule: A value set by dragging or by keys SHOULD report a live change on every step and a separate commit when the gesture ends: on the pointer's release, and on each key press.
rules.why: An app that saves, fetches or records history on every pointermove floods; one that waits for a release never hears a keyboard user, whose every key is a whole gesture.

validated.where: a two-axis colour plane built from two range inputs, React, vitest with happy-dom
validated.finding: Before the change a key on the plane changed the value but reported no commit; after it, each key reports one commit and a drag reports one when let go.
validated.check: unit test "keys on the plane end each change; a drag ends when it is let go" fails on the build before the change (re-run at its parent commit) and passes after

validated.where: a number field scrubbed by dragging its label, and a colour strip dragged with the pointer, web components, headless Chromium with page.mouse and the keyboard
validated.finding: While dragging only input events fired, and the release fired one change; a key step fired one input and one change
validated.check: the scrub test's event log (every entry but the last an input, the last a change) and "the change fires once, on release"; fails on the code before the change (negative control run by the build session, not re-run here)

rules.rule: A table's drop line SHOULD span the visible part of the table across the reorder axis: for a column from the top of the header to the bottom of the last visible row, for a row across the visible width of the scroll box with its terminal mark inside that width.
rules.why: The user looks at any row while carrying a column and at any column while carrying a row. A line as long as one header cell is out of sight for most of the table, and a row line laid in the scrolled content starts off-screen once the box is scrolled sideways.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: an HTML table of 6 columns and 8 rows in a scroll box, with a sticky header row and a sticky first column, columns reordered by the header and rows by a handle; headless Chromium 159 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only
validated.finding: Screenshot pixels on the landing boundary were the line colour in the header, in the second body row and 3px above the visible bottom (column), and over the sticky column and 10px inside the visible right edge with the box scrolled 120px sideways (row), in both engines.
validated.check: "col: the line runs from the header top to the last visible row, over the sticky header"; the negative control drew the line the height of the header only. "row: the line spans the visible width, above the sticky column and the lifted row, when the box is scrolled sideways"; the negative control laid the line in the scrolled content

rules.rule: A table's drop line MUST paint above the sticky cells and above the lifted cells.
rules.why: Sticky cells carry a z-index, so a line drawn in the content passes under them. And cells share a boundary, so a column or row grabbed near its middle always overlaps the boundary it will land on: a line under the lifted cells is hidden exactly when it is needed.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: an HTML table of 6 columns and 8 rows in a scroll box, with a sticky header row and a sticky first column, columns reordered by the header and rows by a handle; headless Chromium 159 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only
validated.finding: A fixed-position line above every table layer showed on the boundary inside the sticky header. A line in the scrolled content at z-index 0 did not: the pixel was the header paint where the lifted header did not cover it, and the lifted paint where it did. For a row the lifted cells always covered the boundary, so "above the sticky column" was only shown together with "above the lifted row".
validated.check: "col: the line paints over the sticky header" (grabbed near the trailing end so the lifted header does not cover the boundary); the negative control put the line in the scrolled content under the sticky cells. Joint evidence for a row: "row: the line spans the visible width, above the sticky column and the lifted row, when the box is scrolled sideways"

rules.rule: The edge of a sticky header MUST be measured from a sticky cell, never from its row or section.
rules.why: Only the cells are sticky. The row keeps its place in the scrolled content, so its box leaves the scroll box as soon as the table is scrolled; every length taken from it (line start, autoscroll band, pointer clamp) is then wrong.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: an HTML table of 6 columns and 8 rows in a scroll box, with a sticky header row and a sticky first column, columns reordered by the header and rows by a handle; headless Chromium 159 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only
validated.finding: Found as a bug in the first build: with the box scrolled down 150px the header row measured top -5px while its sticky cells sat at 57px, in both engines; the row autoscroll band and the column line start were both taken from it.
validated.check: "col: the line stays on the sticky header when the box is scrolled down"; the negative control measured the header row instead of a sticky header cell

rules.rule: Where sticky cells cover a side of the scroll box, the autoscroll edge band MUST start at their inner edge, not at the edge of the scroll box.
rules.why: A 40px band measured from the box lies wholly under a sticky column or header that is wider than 40px. The pointer has to be carried over the pinned cells before anything scrolls, and columns hidden behind them cannot be reached as landing places.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: an HTML table of 6 columns and 8 rows in a scroll box, with a sticky header row and a sticky first column, columns reordered by the header and rows by a handle; headless Chromium 159 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only
validated.finding: With the box scrolled, holding the pointer 20px inside the inner edge of the sticky column (172px from the box edge) or of the sticky header (60px from it) scrolled the box back, in both engines.
validated.check: "col: the near edge band starts at the sticky column's inner edge" and "row: the near edge band starts at the sticky header's inner edge"; the negative control measured the band from the scroll box's own edge

rules.rule: While a drag scrolls its scroll box, the lifted item MUST stay under the pointer: the scroll distance since pick-up is added to its translate.
rules.why: The lifted cells live in the scrolled content. Without the correction they slide away from the pointer by the distance scrolled. Not specific to tables; the existing autoscroll rule only says to re-evaluate the target.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: an HTML table of 6 columns and 8 rows in a scroll box, with a sticky header row and a sticky first column, columns reordered by the header and rows by a handle; headless Chromium 159 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only
validated.finding: After 40px or more of autoscroll the lifted header's (or row's) offset from the pointer equalled the offset at the press within 1px, in both engines; without the correction it was off by the scrolled distance (40px).
validated.check: "col: the lifted cells stay under the pointer while the box scrolls" and "row: the lifted cells stay under the pointer while the box scrolls"; the negative control left the scroll delta out of the translate

rules.rule: Lifted cells SHOULD be given a stacking position above the sticky cells (a positioned cell with a z-index higher than theirs).
rules.why: translate alone creates a stacking context at z-index auto, which paints under any sticky cell that has a z-index: the lifted column slides under the pinned column and the lifted row under the header, and disappears.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: an HTML table of 6 columns and 8 rows in a scroll box, with a sticky header row and a sticky first column, columns reordered by the header and rows by a handle; headless Chromium 159 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only
validated.finding: With position and z-index above the sticky cells, the pixel of a lifted cell carried over the pinned column and over the sticky header was the lifted paint in both engines; with translate alone it was the sticky cell. Whether a lifted column should rather be clamped at the pinned column was not tested.
validated.check: "col: the lifted cells paint above the sticky column" and "row: the lifted cells paint above the sticky header"; the negative control removed position and z-index from the lifted cells

rules.rule: A column reorder MUST move the header cell and the cell of every row together, so each row keeps its cells in the header order.
rules.why: A column exists only as one cell per row. Moving the header alone puts every value under the wrong heading with nothing visibly broken.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: an HTML table of 6 columns and 8 rows in a scroll box, with a sticky header row and a sticky first column, columns reordered by the header and rows by a handle; headless Chromium 159 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only
validated.finding: After a column drop every body row listed its cells in the same order as the header row, in both engines.
validated.check: "col: every row keeps its cells in the header order after a column drop"; the negative control moved the header cell only

rules.rule: The click that follows the release after an Escape cancel MUST be swallowed too.
rules.why: Escape ends the drag while the button is still down. Its release is then an ordinary click on whatever is under the pointer: here it sorted the table by the column just put back, or opened the row's Move menu. Not specific to tables.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: an HTML table of 6 columns and 8 rows in a scroll box, with a sticky header row and a sticky first column, columns reordered by the header and rows by a handle; headless Chromium 159 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only
validated.finding: After Escape during a short carry, releasing the button over the pressed header left the table unsorted and, for a row, opened no menu; the next real click still worked. Both engines.
validated.check: "col: the release after an Escape cancel does not click the part under it" and "row: the release after an Escape cancel does not click the part under it"; the negative control did not swallow the click after the cancelled press's release

validated.where: a shared pointer-drag helper on Pointer Events used by a canvas of nodes with ports (a link drawn from a port to a port) and by plain handles, light DOM and shadow DOM, headless Chromium with page.mouse and the keyboard
validated.finding: After Escape during a short carry, releasing over the pressed handle or port produced no click, so a port was not picked; the next click did. The helper keeps the pointer id of a press cancelled with the button down and swallows the click after that pointer's release, for one task
validated.check: "the release after an Escape cancel does not click; the next click does" for a handle and for a port; fails on the code before the change (negative control run by the build session, not re-run here)

rules.rule: A live drag MUST cancel when pointer capture is lost without a release, and MUST listen for lostpointercapture at the document: when the capturing element leaves the DOM the event fires there, not on the element.
rules.why: A re-render that replaces the dragged node takes its capture with it. Listeners on the element then never hear the release and the drag stays live; listeners on the window carry on with a lifted item that is no longer drawn and commit a move nobody saw.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: a sortable list of six rows dragged by a handle that captures the pointer, with its move, up and cancel listeners on the handle and, in a second run, on the window; every row replaced by a new node mid-drag, as a data refresh does; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse
validated.finding: lostpointercapture fired once, at the document with the document as its target, and never on the removed handle. Without a cancel on it, the drag with listeners on the handle was still live after the release, and the drag with listeners on the window committed a reorder of a row that showed no lift. Hearing the event on the handle only changed nothing. With the cancel at the document the drag ended before the release, fired a cancel and no change, said so in the live region, and the next drag worked. Both engines.
validated.check: "drag: a row re-rendered mid-drag ends the drag at once, and the next drag works", once with listeners on the handle and once on the window; the negative controls were no lostpointercapture listener, and the listener on the handle only

validated.where: a shared pointer-drag helper used on a light-DOM handle and on a handle inside a shadow root, and by a number field whose label scrubs it; the pressed node replaced by a clone mid-drag; headless Chromium with page.mouse
validated.finding: Both cancelled before the release, with no drop and no change; the scrubbed number showed its first value again; the next drag worked. A document-level lostpointercapture listener heard the event for the shadow-root node
validated.check: "the captured node re-rendered mid-drag cancels at once; the release drops nothing; the next drag works" in both roots, and "a scrub whose letter is re-rendered mid-drag puts the value back at once, with no change"; fails on the code before the change (negative control run by the build session, not re-run here)

rules.rule: The non-passive touchmove listener that cancels the scroll MUST be on the handle before the press begins (added when the handle is mounted); it MUST NOT be added in the pointerdown handler or when the drag goes live.
rules.why: Touch events stay with the node the finger landed on. When the press re-renders that node, a listener added afterwards to the node now in the document hears nothing, and one added to the pressed node hears touchmoves that can no longer be cancelled: the page scrolls and the drag ends in pointercancel. Where nothing re-renders a late listener works, so the fault shows only once a re-render is added. Touch events stay with the node where the touch began, so a listener delegated to a root misses a handle that is replaced during the press.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: a sortable list of six rows in a page that scrolls, each dragged by a handle (mouse past 4px, finger after 250ms), with a keyboard mode on the handle and Move up and Move down buttons; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and page.keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only; the pointerdown handler replaced every row with a new node in the second run
validated.finding: Chromium only. With the pressed handle replaced during the press: listener at mount, scrollY 0 and the row moved; listener added at pointerdown or at go-live, the page scrolled 91px and the drag ended in pointercancel (0 touchmoves heard on the new node; 6 heard on the pressed node, none cancelable). With no re-render the late listeners worked. A passive listener failed on both pages. WebKit could not be tested: its driver has a tap only.
validated.check: "touch: the same, where the press re-renders every row (the pressed handle is replaced)"; negative controls: the listener added at pointerdown (to the new node, to the pressed node), at go-live, passive, and absent

rules.note: Validated by touch in one engine only: the other engine's driver cannot move a finger. The source states the cause for every engine: a touch's events stay with the element it started on, even after that element leaves the document, and it advises putting touch listeners on the target itself where it may be removed while touched.

rules.rule: The drop line MUST NOT show in the two gaps beside the dragged item's own slot, where a release moves nothing.
rules.why: A line says the item will land there. In its own gaps the release is a no-op, so a line there promises a move that does not happen.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: a sortable list of six rows in a page that scrolls, each dragged by a handle (mouse past 4px, finger after 250ms), with a keyboard mode on the handle and Move up and Move down buttons; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and page.keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only
validated.finding: With the line hidden in the row's own gaps a line at release always meant a change event. With the line shown there, it showed at release and the release fired no change and moved nothing. Both engines.
validated.check: "own gap: a line shows only where a release would move the row"; negative control: the line also shown in the row's own gaps

rules.rule: A drop line MUST take no room in the layout: in the flow it is a zero-height box whose stroke is drawn outside it, and inside a container spaced by gap it MUST be positioned out of the flow.
rules.why: A line with height pushes the rows below it each time it appears, and in a flex or grid container any item, even an empty one, adds a gap; the rows then move under the pointer while the user aims.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: a sortable list of six rows in a page that scrolls, each dragged by a handle (mouse past 4px, finger after 250ms), with a keyboard mode on the handle and Move up and Move down buttons; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and page.keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only
validated.finding: A zero-height line between rows spaced by margins moved no row (0px) and left the list 284px high; a line 2px high moved the rows below 2px. In a flex column with a 4px gap the zero-height line moved them 4px and the 2px line 6px. Both engines.
validated.check: "line: showing the line moves no row (rows spaced by margins)"; negative control: a line 2px high in the flow; the flex-gap run was an observation

rules.rule: A view transition that animates a reorder MUST be scoped to the list (element.startViewTransition) and MUST be left out where the engine has no scoped transition; it MUST NOT be a document-wide transition.
rules.why: While a document-wide transition runs, the hit test anywhere on the page returns the root element, so every press on the page is lost until the animation ends.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: a sortable list of six rows in a page that scrolls, each dragged by a handle (mouse past 4px, finger after 250ms), with a keyboard mode on the handle and Move up and Move down buttons; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and page.keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only; a drop animated for 600ms
validated.finding: With document.startViewTransition, 120ms after the drop the hit test at a button elsewhere on the page returned the root element and a mouse click on it was not counted, in both engines. Scoped to the list (Chromium), the click was counted while 36 transition animations ran. WebKit 27.2 has no element.startViewTransition; with the transition left out there the click was counted.
validated.check: "view transition: a press elsewhere on the page right after a drop lands"; negative control: a document-wide transition

rules.rule: In a virtualised list the dragged item's node MUST stay in the DOM for as long as the drag is live, however far its slot scrolls out of the rendered window.
rules.why: The node holds the pointer capture. When the window recycles it the capture is lost, and a drag that cancels on lost capture (drag.lost-capture) ends the moment the user scrolls far enough to need it.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: 200 rows in a 308px scroll box with about ten in the DOM, a row dragged by a handle that captures the pointer, the box scrolled 880px by the mouse wheel mid-drag; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse
validated.finding: With the dragged row kept in the DOM the release moved it from index 2 to 22. Rendered like any other row it was removed when its slot left the window, capture was lost and the drag was cancelled with nothing moved. Both engines. Touch and autoscroll were not tried.
validated.check: "virtual: a row whose slot has scrolled out of the window is still dropped where it is let go"; negative control: the dragged row unmounts with its slot

rules.rule: A row that can take an item both onto itself and beside itself MUST split its box along the drag axis: the middle (about half) means onto it, shown by a tint and no line, and the outer parts (about a quarter each) mean before and after, shown by the line.
rules.why: With no middle zone a closed or empty container cannot be dropped into; with the whole row meaning onto, a place between two such rows cannot be reached.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: a tree of items and folders with 36px rows and 24px of indent a level, rows dragged with the mouse; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse
validated.finding: With a middle half and outer quarters, a release on the middle of a closed folder put the item in it and a release in the upper quarter put the item before it, between two folders. With two halves the item could not be put into the closed folder; with the whole row meaning onto, it could not be put between the two folders. Both engines.
validated.check: "zones: the middle of a closed folder row takes the item into the folder" (control: two halves), "zones: the upper quarter of a folder row places the item before it, between two folders" (control: the whole row means onto)

rules.rule: In a tree, where a gap could belong to more than one level (under the last child of an open branch), the pointer's position along the indent axis MUST pick the level, and the line MUST start at that level's indent.
rules.why: The gap under a branch's last child is both the end of the branch and the place after it. If it always takes one level, the other place cannot be reached by a drag.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: a tree of items and folders with 36px rows and 24px of indent a level, rows dragged with the mouse; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse
validated.finding: In the gap under an open folder's last child, the pointer at the outer indent placed the item after the folder (line at depth 0) and at the inner indent made it the last child (line at depth 1). With the gap always taking the level of the row above, the place after the folder could not be reached. Both engines.
validated.check: "depth: in the gap under a folder's last child, the pointer at the outer level places the item after the folder"; negative control: the gap always takes the level of the row above

rules.rule: A target that would refuse the dragged item MUST show no line and no tint, and a release on it MUST put the item back and say so.
rules.why: A tint or a line says the item will land there. On a target that refuses it the release changes nothing, so the indicator promises a move that does not happen.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: a tree of items and folders with 36px rows and 24px of indent a level, rows dragged with the mouse; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse; one folder refuses every item
validated.finding: Over the refusing folder nothing was shown, and the release fired a cancel, moved nothing and announced the item put back. With the folder tinted like an accepting one, the tint showed at release and the release still moved nothing. Both engines.
validated.check: "refused: over a folder that takes nothing, nothing is shown; what shows at release is what the release does"; negative control: the refusing folder is tinted

rules.rule: When the save that follows an optimistic drop fails, the order MUST be put back as it was before the drop (from a snapshot taken then), the failure MUST be announced, and focus MUST stay on the item.
rules.why: A drop shown at once and never saved leaves the screen showing an order the server does not hold, and nothing tells the user.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: a sortable list of six rows in a page that scrolls, each dragged by a handle (mouse past 4px, finger after 250ms), with a keyboard mode on the handle and Move up and Move down buttons; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and page.keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only; the save after a drop refused after 200ms
validated.finding: With the restore the list returned to the order the server held and said "Could not save. Snare put back, position 2 of 6", with focus on the row. Without it the list showed the row at position 4 while the server held it at position 2 and nothing was said. Both engines.
validated.check: "save: when the save is refused the list goes back to what the server holds, says so and keeps focus on the row"; negative control: no restore

rules.rule: A press on a slider's handle MUST NOT change the value: the drag keeps the pointer's offset from the handle's centre. A press on the track outside the handle SHOULD jump the handle to the pointer.
rules.why: A press that jumps to the pointer moves the value by the few pixels between where the press landed and the handle's centre, so a click meant to grab it changes it.

validated.where: a vertical fader with a cap on a recessed slot and a readout, web component, headless Chromium with page.mouse
validated.finding: A click 4px off the cap's centre left the value unchanged; a drag then moved it from that offset; a click on the bare slot below the cap set the minimum
validated.check: "a press on the cap grabs it where it is: no jump" and "a press at the foot of the slot jumps to the floor"; fails on the code before the change (negative control run by the build session, not re-run here)

rules.rule: A control whose range spans two or more decades SHOULD use a logarithmic taper, and its indicator, marks, pointer drag and keys MUST all use the same one; an arrow key MUST step a fraction of the travel (about a hundredth), not one unit of the value, once the range holds more than about 200 steps.
rules.why: On a linear travel of 20 to 20000, everything below 200 takes under 1% of the sweep, so a drag cannot place it, and an arrow moves 1 of 19,980 steps.

validated.where: a knob over a cutoff of 20 Hz to 20 kHz with eleven lit marks, web component, headless Chromium with page.mouse, the keyboard and the wheel
validated.finding: At 2400 Hz the indicator sat at the log angle (within 0.5°) with seven of eleven marks lit; a 40px drag up raised the value by more than ×1.5 and turned the indicator by about a tenth of the sweep; ArrowDown lowered it by more than 5%, not by 1 Hz; Home and End gave 20 and 20000. On the linear code before the change the indicator and marks were off and an arrow moved 1 Hz
validated.check: "a log cutoff turns by drag, keys and wheel"; fails on the code before the change (negative control run by the build session, not re-run here)

rules.rule: Everything a drag does MUST also be possible with single-pointer actions that are not drags (WCAG 2.5.7, AA): typically a Move control on the item opening a menu of destinations (other containers, up, down), or select-then-arrow buttons. A swipe does not count, and keyboard support does not satisfy it.
rules.why: People using trackballs, head pointers, eye gaze or voice-driven pointers cannot drag; W3C failure F108 names a kanban without a click alternative.

validated.where: a web-component kanban board, Chromium (Playwright)
validated.finding: A Move key on the card under the pointer or with focus opens a menu of the other lanes, Move up and Move down; choosing one moves the card with no drag.
validated.check: browser test clicks the key and a menu item

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: an HTML table of 6 columns and 8 rows in a scroll box, with a sticky header row and a sticky first column, columns reordered by the header and rows by a handle; headless Chromium 159 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only
validated.finding: Holds unchanged for a table column reordered by its header and for a row reordered by a handle.
validated.check: "col: clicks alone move it through the Move menu, with the same change event" and "row: clicks alone move it through the Move menu, with the same change event" (control: no Move control). The menu fires the same change event as a drop.

validated.where: a number that is set by dragging across it (a step per 2px) and starts typing on a click, with a minus and a plus key at its two ends; web component, headless Chromium with page.mouse
validated.finding: One click on the plus key raised the value by one step, left focus on the field and did not start typing; with a fine pointer the keys sat hidden until hover or focus
validated.check: "one click on + raises the value one step" for each look; fails on the code before the change (negative control run by the build session, not re-run here)

validated.where: a canvas of nodes with output and input ports joined by cords drawn by dragging, web component, headless Chromium with page.mouse and the keyboard
validated.finding: A click on a port picked it and a click on a port of the other kind joined the two, with the same data change as the drag; Enter did the same by keyboard; Escape dropped the pick; Delete on an input port removed its links; a link made by dragging picked no port
validated.check: "two clicks connect: a port, then a port of the other kind" and "a drag from an output port to an input port makes a cord"; fails on the code before the change (negative control run by the build session, not re-run here)

rules.rule: The Move control MUST name the item it acts on ("Move <item>"), MUST be reachable by Tab from the item, and after a move focus MUST return to the moved item, or to a sensible neighbour if it no longer exists.
rules.why: A row of identical "Move" buttons is unusable by name; focus left on a control that just re-rendered elsewhere is lost.

validated.where: a web-component kanban board, Chromium (Playwright)
validated.finding: Tab from a card reaches "Move <card>"; Enter opens the menu on its first item; Enter moves the card and focus is on the card.
validated.check: browser test by keyboard; fails when the menu cannot find its focused item (shadow.active-element)

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: an HTML table of 6 columns and 8 rows in a scroll box, with a sticky header row and a sticky first column, columns reordered by the header and rows by a handle; headless Chromium 159 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only
validated.finding: Holds unchanged for a table column reordered by its header and for a row reordered by a handle.
validated.check: "col: Tab reaches the Move control" and "row: Tab reaches the Move control" (control: tabindex -1), "col: keys move it through the menu and focus returns to its Move control in the new place" and "row: keys move it through the menu and focus returns to its Move control in the new place" (control: no focus call after the move; focus fell to the body), "col: each Move control has a name of its own that holds its header's text" and "row: each Move control has a name of its own that holds its header's text" (control: every control named "Move"). Reading used: "the moved item" is its Move control, which sits inside the moved header or row, so a second Enter moves it again. WebKit reached the buttons with Option+Tab only.

rules.rule: A keyboard drag mode (a key picks up, arrows carry, a key drops, Escape cancels) MAY be offered beside the Move menu; it MUST NOT be the only non-pointer way.
rules.why: Primer and React Aria build keyboard drag modes; Atlassian advises menus instead, since arrow carrying is hard without sight, needs a mode switch in JAWS and takes many keystrokes.

rules.rule: The Move control of a column MUST be named from its header text and the word column, and that of a row from its row header cell and the word row, never from an index.
rules.why: Rows and columns of one table share one set of controls, so each name has to say which axis it moves. An index names a place, not a row: it goes stale on the first reorder.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: an HTML table of 6 columns and 8 rows in a scroll box, with a sticky header row and a sticky first column, columns reordered by the header and rows by a handle; headless Chromium 159 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only
validated.finding: All 13 Move controls had distinct names that held their header text ("Move Team column", "Move Chen Wei row"), and each row kept its name after another row was dragged past it. Both engines. That the word "column" or "row" is needed was not shown by a colliding case; only reading by a screen reader would show how the names sound.
validated.check: "col: each Move control has a name of its own that holds its header's text" and "row: each Move control has a name of its own that holds its header's text"; the negative control named every control "Move". "row: the Move control is named from the row header cell and keeps the name when the row moves"; the negative control named rows by their index at render

rules.rule: A row's drag handle MAY also be its Move control: a click or Enter opens the Move menu, a drag past the threshold reorders.
rules.why: One control per row instead of two keeps the row narrow and the tab order short. It depends on the activation threshold (a click stays a click) and on swallowing the click after a drop and after a cancel (the menu must not open).

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: an HTML table of 6 columns and 8 rows in a scroll box, with a sticky header row and a sticky first column, columns reordered by the header and rows by a handle; headless Chromium 159 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only
validated.finding: One button per row served as handle and menu trigger in both engines: a 2px press opened the menu, a carry reordered, and neither a drop nor a cancel opened the menu.
validated.check: "row: a 2px press is a click, not a drag" (negative control: no threshold), "row: the click after a drop is swallowed" (negative control: no click swallowing; the menu opened), "row: Tab reaches the Move control"

rules.rule: A two-axis plane (a thumb dragged in two dimensions) MUST hold one native range input per axis, each named, so both axes are operable by keyboard and present in the accessibility tree; the plane SHOULD be one tab stop, with the focused input also taking the other axis's two arrow keys, so each arrow moves the thumb the way it points.
rules.why: A plane built on pointer handlers alone cannot be operated by keyboard and is not in the accessibility tree (WCAG 2.1.1). A native range input moves on all four arrows, so with two independent inputs ArrowUp moves the thumb sideways and the other axis needs a second Tab.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: an OKLCH colour picker with a 200px chroma by lightness plane, a row per channel (range input and number input) and a text field for a typed colour; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by the real keyboard and mouse; the accessibility tree read by CDP in Chromium and by a computed aria snapshot in WebKit
validated.finding: With a range input per axis and one stop, Tab stopped once on the plane, ArrowRight moved chroma alone and the thumb right, ArrowUp moved lightness alone and the thumb up, and the tree held two named sliders. As a div with pointer handlers Tab passed the plane, no key changed the colour and the tree held nothing inside it. With two independent stops ArrowUp moved chroma and the thumb 2px to the right. Both engines.
validated.check: "plane: it is one tab stop between its neighbours", "plane: both axes are sliders in the accessibility tree, named, each value text naming the other axis" and "plane: from its one stop, left and right move chroma alone and up and down move lightness alone"; the negative controls were a plane with no inputs, and two inputs each in the tab order taking only their own keys

rules.note: The sources state keyboard operability and the keys of one slider; neither states one tab stop for a plane. The APG multi-thumb slider keeps every thumb in the tab sequence, but its thumbs share one axis.

rules.rule: A colour picker whose plane steps more coarsely than the values it holds MUST also give each channel a control of its own that reaches every value: a number field, or a slider at the value's own step.
rules.why: A plane steps by about a pixel, so a value between two of its steps cannot be reached on it by key or pointer; the user who was given an exact colour cannot enter it.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: an OKLCH colour picker with a 200px chroma by lightness plane, a row per channel (range input and number input) and a text field for a typed colour; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by the real keyboard and mouse
validated.finding: With a number field per channel L 0.5, C 0.123, H 200 was entered in 17 key presses. With only the plane (chroma step 0.002) and a hue slider the keyboard stopped at chroma 0.124 after 222 presses. With a slider per channel at step 0.001 and no number field the colour was reached exactly, in 393 presses. Both engines.
validated.check: "channels: an exact colour (L 0.5, C 0.123, H 200) is entered with the keyboard"; the negative control removed the channel rows and left the plane and a hue slider

rules.rule: A move control that acts on a multi-select list MUST move every selected option, in list order, whichever one has focus; with nothing selected it SHOULD move nothing and say so with aria-disabled.
rules.why: A move that takes the focused option leaves the rest behind still marked selected, so the list shows a selection the move ignored. A move with nothing selected takes an option the user never chose.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a transfer list of two multi-select listboxes (focus on the option, one roving tab stop each) with two move buttons between them; headless Chromium 158.0.8127.18 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS, driven by page.mouse and the keyboard (Option+Tab in WebKit)
validated.finding: With three options selected, three moved; with the move taking the focused option, one moved and two stayed marked selected. With nothing selected nothing moved; without that guard the current option moved while the button said it was disabled. Both engines.
validated.check: "transfer: the move button moves every selected option, in list order" and "transfer: Enter in the list moves every selected option" (control: the move takes the focused option), "transfer: with nothing selected, the move button and Enter move nothing" (control: the move takes the current option when nothing is selected)

rules.rule: A live region MUST announce pick-up, each change of position or container, the drop and a cancel, naming the item, the container and the position ("Snare dropped in Doing, position 3 of 3"); rapid position updates SHOULD be debounced (about 100ms).
rules.why: A drag changes nothing a screen reader reads on its own; repeated rapid announcements interrupt each other.

validated.where: a web-component kanban board, Chromium (Playwright)
validated.finding: Pointer drop, cancel and menu move each announce the card, lane and position.
validated.check: browser test waits for the live region's text

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: an HTML table of 6 columns and 8 rows in a scroll box, with a sticky header row and a sticky first column, columns reordered by the header and rows by a handle; headless Chromium 159 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only
validated.finding: Holds unchanged for a table column reordered by its header and for a row reordered by a handle.
validated.check: "col: pick-up is announced with name and position" and "row: pick-up is announced with name and position", "col: a new landing place is announced while carried" and "row: a new landing place is announced while carried", "col: the drop is announced with name and position" and "row: the drop is announced with name and position", "col: a cancel is announced" and "row: a cancel is announced", "col: a menu move is announced" and "row: a menu move is announced" (control for all: the announcer does nothing). The table has no container to name; the texts name the header and the kind: "Team column dropped, position 4 of 6", "Chen Wei row put back, position 3 of 8".

rules.rule: aria-grabbed and aria-dropeffect MUST NOT be used; state comes from live-region announcements and the item's own role and name.
rules.why: Both are deprecated in ARIA 1.1 and unsupported by assistive technology.

rules.rule: During a keyboard or screen-reader drag across many possible places, everything that is not a valid drop target SHOULD be hidden from assistive technology, and Tab SHOULD move only between valid targets.
rules.why: A touch screen-reader user otherwise swipes past hundreds of unrelated elements to find a target.

rules.rule: A composite value (a range, a value with a validity state) SHOULD be announced once when its state changes, such as a range becoming whole or empty, and never on each key that leaves the state as it was.
rules.why: Announcing per key interrupts the user's own typing echo; announcing nothing leaves a screen reader user unsure the range was taken.

validated.where: a date field and a date range field in a React UI kit, vitest with happy-dom
validated.finding: Keys and a start alone say nothing; the range is said once when both ends are set, and "No dates chosen" once when both are emptied.
validated.check: unit test "announces the range once it is whole, and once both ends are emptied; never per key" fails on the code before the fix (re-run at the fix's parent commit with the new test) and passes after

rules.rule: Each slider of a two-dimensional control (a plane built from two sliders) MUST carry a value text that also names the other axis's value.
rules.why: A screen reader reads one slider at a time, but the position is the pair; with only its own value the user cannot tell where on the plane the thumb is.

validated.where: a lightness by chroma colour plane built from two range inputs, React, vitest with happy-dom
validated.finding: Before the change each axis said only its own value ("51 percent"); after it, "51 percent, chroma 0.120".
validated.check: unit test "the plane is a named group with one tab stop: a chroma axis and a lightness axis on its thumb" fails on the build before the change (re-run at its parent commit) and passes after

rules.rule: An item that folds from a toolbar or segmented control into a menu MUST become the menu item that carries its state: a toggle button a menuitemcheckbox with aria-checked, a radio a menuitemradio with aria-checked inside a named group, and an action a menuitem.
rules.why: A menu's items are menuitem, menuitemcheckbox or menuitemradio, and only the last two have a checked state. A folded toggle or radio written as a plain menuitem still works, but its state has left the accessibility tree: nothing says that it is on, or which of the set is chosen.

validated.where: a toolbar of toggles, an action and a radio group folding into a More menu, headless Chromium (its accessibility tree by CDP and an aria snapshot) and WebKit (aria snapshot)
validated.finding: Six folded items read as menuitemcheckbox, menuitem and grouped menuitemradio with the checked state of their sources, and a state changed in the menu read back from the menu and from the unfolded toolbar. Written as plain menuitems, all six lost their role and the two that were on lost their checked state, in both trees.
validated.check: write every folded item as a plain menuitem: the tree must not match the sources' roles and states

rules.rule: A single-choice control that spills into a menu MUST still say which item is selected while the menu is closed: the selected item SHOULD stay in the row, taking the last place that shows; otherwise the menu's trigger MUST carry the selected item's label.
rules.why: When the selected segment folds like any other, the row shows a radio group with no radio checked and no text naming the choice. Every item can still be reached, but the control's value is hidden until the menu is opened, for a sighted user and in the accessibility tree alike.

validated.where: a five-segment radio group folding into a More menu, headless Chromium and WebKit (aria snapshot and visible text)
validated.finding: With the selected segment kept, the row read Day, Month checked, More. Folded like the rest it read Day, Week, More: no checked radio and no mention of the selected view, also after another was chosen from the menu. Folding it and naming it on the trigger passed. All five views stayed reachable by keyboard in every variant.
validated.check: let the selected segment fold with no label on the trigger: the closed row must not name the selection

rules.rule: When a field changes the value the user typed so that it fits (a colour outside the gamut reduced into it, a number clamped to its range), a live region MUST say once what was changed, from what and to what; a value taken as typed MUST NOT be announced.
rules.why: The field's text is rewritten after the user has finished typing it, so a screen reader user hears their own value and holds another; nothing a screen reader reads on its own reports the rewrite.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: an OKLCH colour picker with a 200px chroma by lightness plane, a row per channel (range input and number input) and a text field for a typed colour; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by the real keyboard and mouse
validated.finding: Typing oklch(0.7 0.4 150) and Enter rewrote the field to oklch(0.7 0.192 150); with the announcement the live region said "Chroma reduced from 0.4 to 0.192 to fit sRGB" once, without it the field changed in silence. A colour inside sRGB was kept as typed and nothing was said. Both engines; a number clamped to its range was not tested.
validated.check: "typed colour: one outside sRGB is fitted, and a live region says what changed" (the negative control fitted the colour and said nothing) and "typed colour: one inside sRGB is kept as typed and nothing is said"

rules.note: WCAG 4.1.3 requires that a status message be exposed through a role or property; it does not say a fit must produce one. Only the colour case was tested.

rules.rule: An item placed by time (an event in a day or week grid, a bar on a timeline) MUST carry its day and start time in its accessible name, in words, beside its title.
rules.why: On screen the day and time are the item's position; a name read out has no position, so two events with one title are the same control twice.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a week time grid of 7 days by 10 hourly slots with six events in it and four outside its hours; headless Chromium 158.0.8127.18 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS, driven by page.mouse and the keyboard (Option+Tab in WebKit)
validated.finding: Two events with one title on two days had different names, each holding the weekday, date and start time; with the title alone both were named the same. Read from Playwright's name computation in both engines and from Chromium's accessibility tree; no screen reader.
validated.check: "scheduler: each event is named with its day and start time, so two events with one title have different names"; the negative control named each event by its title alone

rules.rule: A label that does not fit MUST be clipped by CSS (text-overflow, line-clamp), never cut in script, unless the whole text is also given as the accessible name.
rules.why: Text clipped by CSS stays whole in the accessibility tree; a string cut in script is all there is, so the name read out stops mid-word and the rest is nowhere.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a week time grid of 7 days by 10 hourly slots with six events in it and four outside its hours; headless Chromium 158.0.8127.18 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS, driven by page.mouse and the keyboard (Option+Tab in WebKit)
validated.finding: A title clipped by CSS to 99px of its 359px kept its whole text as the name; the same title cut to 14 characters in script was named by those 14 characters and an ellipsis. Read from Playwright's name computation in both engines and from Chromium's accessibility tree; no screen reader.
validated.check: "scheduler: an event whose title is cut short on screen still has the whole title in its name"; the negative control cut the string in script

rules.rule: Each change between Review and Edit MUST write one message to a status region that names the scope and what happened ("Editing Contact details", "Contact details saved", "Contact details: changes discarded"), and typing in the scope MUST NOT write one.
rules.why: Save and Cancel move focus away from what changed, so the result is said nowhere else. With several sections on a page, a bare "Saved" does not say which one, and two writes for one change are two announcements.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a record of three sections (text fields, a select, a date field with a picker popup, a field with a clear button, a field with steppers), an Edit button per section, Edit, Save and Cancel for the whole record and a New record button; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard
validated.finding: A MutationObserver on the role="status" region recorded exactly one write for each Edit, Save, Cancel and Escape of a section, of the whole record and of a new record, each naming its scope, and none while typing. With no scope in the text, saving two sections gave the same message twice. Both engines. No screen reader was run: what was measured is the write.
validated.check: "announce: Edit, Save and Cancel of a section each write one message that names the section", "announce: the same change in two sections gives two different messages" and "announce: Edit and Save of the whole record, and of a new record, each write one message that names it"; the negative controls wrote no message, wrote it twice, and wrote it without the scope

rules.rule: A chart of discrete points SHOULD be a native table (header cells for series and points, a cell that says a gap in words) and give it a name that states the title, the point count and the unit; it MUST NOT add a live region or a second hidden copy of its data.
rules.why: A table already carries every value, name and gap to the accessibility tree; a second copy drifts, and a live region would say the same thing twice.

validated.where: a bar chart of twelve categorical points in three series drawn as a native table, web component, headless Chromium, read through the accessibility tree; no screen reader
validated.finding: The tree showed a table named with its title, point count and unit, a column header per series with its unit, a row header per point, each row reading its values, a gap read as a word, thirteen rows (the header and twelve), and no Table button
validated.check: "the table is the chart, read through the accessibility tree"; fails on the code before the change (negative control run by the build session, not re-run here)

rules.rule: A chart that is not a table MUST be one focusable group named with its title, point count, unit and each series' range, MUST move a point on the arrow keys and on Home and End, and MUST say each point's value for every series in a live region, a gap in words; its numbers MUST also be reachable as a real table.
rules.why: A drawn line has no values in the accessibility tree; the live region says them as the user moves, and the table is for anyone.

validated.where: a line chart of twelve points in three series with a gap, web component, headless Chromium with the real keyboard; no screen reader
validated.finding: After focus the live region said the first point's value for every series with its unit; after five ArrowRight it said the sixth, with the gap as a word; End and Home moved to the ends; the group's name held the title, point count, unit, each series' range and its gaps; a Table button was in the tree
validated.check: "arrows read each point into the live region"; fails on the code before the change (negative control run by the build session, not re-run here)

rules.rule: A board, list, table of rows or other composite whose parts are reached by arrows SHOULD be one Tab stop (roving tabindex): the last focused item has tabindex 0, the rest -1, and a pressed item becomes the stop.
rules.why: Tab through every card of every lane is unusable; arrows move within the composite.

validated.where: a web-component kanban board, Chromium (Playwright)
validated.finding: Shift+Tab into the board lands on its one stop; arrows move between cards and lanes.
validated.check: browser tests titled by key

validated.where: a table of twelve rows used as a chart, web component, headless Chromium with the real keyboard
validated.finding: Tab landed on row 0; two ArrowRight then ArrowLeft landed on row 1; End landed on row 11, the only row with tabindex 0; the next Tab left the table
validated.check: "one tab stop, arrows move between rows"; fails on the code before the change (negative control run by the build session, not re-run here)

rules.rule: In a list that keeps focus on its container (aria-activedescendant), a pressed option MUST become the active option; the active option's paint MUST differ from the selected paint and MUST NOT be the pressed paint; and in a multi-select list it SHOULD show only while the list has focus.
rules.why: A focus handler that picks the first option runs before the click, so without the click moving it the first row always looks current; a cursor painted as pressed, or left showing after focus moves away, reads as the selection while the real selection shows only its mark.

validated.where: a two-list transfer component (multi-select listboxes), Chromium (Playwright)
validated.finding: Clicking the third option left the first one painted as current; after the fix the clicked option is the cursor, the cursor is a light fill with no sunk shadow, it disappears when focus leaves, and a marked row ignores hover.
validated.check: browser test; all four checks fail on the old build

rules.rule: When a control's focusable host also holds printed parts (a scale, marks, labels), the focus ring SHOULD go on the part you touch (a fader's cap, a knob's body), with the host's own outline removed, so the ring marks what keys and pointer act on.
rules.why: A ring around the whole control, scale included, frames dead space and reads as a selection box, not as the thing that moves.

validated.where: a fader and knob web components, Chromium (Playwright)
validated.finding: With keyboard focus the ring now circles the knob body and the fader cap, and the host carries no outline.
validated.check: browser test reads the ring on the touch part and none on the host; fails on the old build

validated.where: a rotary switch whose focus sits on a hidden radio, with a knob body as the touched part, web component, headless Chromium
validated.finding: After an arrow key the knob's outline was solid; after a mouse press on the knob it was none
validated.check: "the focus ring is on the knob, from the keyboard only"; fails on the code before the change (negative control run by the build session, not re-run here)

rules.rule: A control placed inside a listbox option for pointer use MUST be out of the tab order, named, and its action MUST also be reachable by a key on the listbox.
rules.why: A listbox does not support interacting with elements inside an option, so a tab stop inside one is unreachable or unannounced; the key on the list is the keyboard path, the name is for voice control.
rules.note: Where the rows need real interactive children, the APG points to the grid pattern instead of a listbox.

rules.rule: A scroller under sticky or fixed bands (a header, a footer, a banner) SHOULD set scroll-padding to the bands' measured heights, so a focused element is never scrolled under them.
rules.why: Focus moved by Tab scrolls the element just into the scroller's edge, which is under the band; WCAG 2.4.11 (AA) fails when the focused element is entirely hidden.

rules.rule: A feed (role feed of focusable articles) SHOULD move focus to the next and previous article on Page Down and Page Up, and out of the feed on Control+End and Control+Home.
rules.why: A feed can be endless and loads as it scrolls, so Tab through every link of every article never reaches what is after it.
rules.note: The APG recommends these keys or a comparable set, since the feed role has no established convention.

rules.rule: After a drop that re-inserts the moved nodes, focus MUST be put back on the pressed part of the moved item.
rules.why: Removing and re-inserting a cell that holds the focused part drops focus to the body in both engines, so the next key press goes nowhere. The same re-insertion is why no click was dispatched after such a drop.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: an HTML table of 6 columns and 8 rows in a scroll box, with a sticky header row and a sticky first column, columns reordered by the header and rows by a handle; headless Chromium 159 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only
validated.finding: After a drop that moved the column or row, the focused element was the body until the drop code focused the pressed part again; with that call it was the sort button or handle inside the item at its new index. Both engines. A move that keeps the nodes attached (moveBefore, CSS order) was not tested.
validated.check: "col: focus is still on the moved item's part after a drop that re-inserts it" and "row: focus is still on the moved item's part after a drop that re-inserts it"; the negative control removed the focus call after the move

rules.rule: When the part that holds a roving tab stop is hidden (an item that folds into an overflow menu), the stop MUST move to a part that still shows, such as the menu's trigger, and focus MUST move with it when the hidden part had focus.
rules.why: A hidden part cannot take focus. If the only tabindex 0 is on it, Tab passes the whole toolbar; if it had focus, focus falls to the body and the arrow keys stop working.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a toolbar of six buttons with one roving tab stop, whose buttons fold into a More menu as a ResizeObserver reports less room; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by the keyboard and a real viewport resize
validated.finding: With the stop left on a folded button, focus fell to the body when the focused button folded, and Shift+Tab from the next control skipped the toolbar and landed on the control before it. With the stop and focus moved to the More trigger, focus stayed in the toolbar, ArrowLeft reached the last showing button, Shift+Tab landed on the trigger and one visible tab stop remained. Both engines.
validated.check: "toolbar: when the focused item folds, focus moves to the More trigger and the arrows still work" and "toolbar: after its stop folds, Shift+Tab from the next control still lands in the toolbar"; the negative control left the stop and focus on the folded item

rules.rule: When the focused option is moved out of a list, focus MUST stay in that list: on the first option after it that stays, else the last one before it, else the list itself, which then is the tab stop.
rules.why: The moved node leaves the list with focus on it, so focus falls to the body and the next arrow key goes nowhere. Staying in the list lets the user move one option after another.
rules.note: alternative.trigger and focus.after-drop put focus on the moved item when it stays in view of the same control; this rule is for an item that leaves its list. The APG example states the next-option part only; the previous option and the empty list are from the test.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a transfer list of two multi-select listboxes (focus on the option, one roving tab stop each) with two move buttons between them; headless Chromium 158.0.8127.18 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS, driven by page.mouse and the keyboard (Option+Tab in WebKit)
validated.finding: After a move focus was on the next option, on the previous one when the last moved, and on the list when it emptied; ArrowDown went on from there. Without the focus call it was on the body in all four cases, in both engines.
