validated.check: "transfer: after a move by Enter, focus is on the next option of the source list and the arrows go on from it", "transfer: when the last option moves, focus is on the one before it", "transfer: when every option moves, focus is on the empty list, which is still a tab stop", "transfer: after a move by the button with the mouse, focus is on the next option of the source list"; the negative control removed the focus call after the move

rules.rule: A button that acts on a list's selection while the list has focus SHOULD cancel mousedown (preventDefault), so a press leaves focus on the list's option; it MUST stay reachable by Tab and work by key.
rules.why: Without it a press takes focus from the list: to the button in Chromium, and to the body in WebKit, which does not focus a button on a click, so the focus rule after the move has nothing to go on and the keyboard user starts again from the top of the page. The selection itself is state, not focus, and survives either way.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a transfer list of two multi-select listboxes (focus on the option, one roving tab stop each) with two move buttons between them; headless Chromium 158.0.8127.18 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS, driven by page.mouse and the keyboard (Option+Tab in WebKit)
validated.finding: With mousedown cancelled, focus stayed on the option through the press in both engines and moved to the next option after the move. Without it focus went to the button in Chromium and to the body in WebKit, where it stayed after the move (6 Tab presses to return). The selection was kept in both engines either way.
validated.check: "transfer: a mouse press on the move button leaves focus and the cursor in the list, and the arrows go on after the move"; the negative control did not cancel mousedown. "transfer: a mouse press on the move button never leaves focus on the body" failed under the control in WebKit only

rules.rule: A count that stands for items not shown ("3 more") MUST be a button that opens them, named with what it counts and where, with aria-expanded; opening MUST move focus to the first of them and Escape MUST return it.
rules.why: As text with a click handler the count is no tab stop, so the items behind it cannot be reached from the keyboard at all (WCAG 2.1.1).

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a week time grid of 7 days by 10 hourly slots with six events in it and four outside its hours; headless Chromium 158.0.8127.18 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS, driven by page.mouse and the keyboard (Option+Tab in WebKit)
validated.finding: As a button the count was the third tab stop; Enter opened the three events with focus on the first and Escape returned it. As a span with a click handler Tab never reached it in eight presses, though a mouse click opened the same list. Both engines.
validated.check: "scheduler: the off-window count is reached by Tab, Enter opens the hidden events with focus on the first, Escape returns"; the negative control made the count a span with the same click handler

rules.rule: A day or week time grid SHOULD be one tab stop that takes the APG data grid keys: arrows move one slot or one day and stop at the edge, Home and End go to the first and last day of the row, Control with them to the first and last cell, Page Up and Page Down move a set number of slots; a cell that holds one event puts focus on the event.
rules.why: A week of hourly slots is 70 cells or more: as tab stops they stand between the keyboard user and everything after the grid, and an empty slot that takes no focus cannot be chosen at all.
rules.note: date.grid-keys covers a calendar of days, where Page Up and Page Down change the month; here they move within the day.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a week time grid of 7 days by 10 hourly slots with six events in it and four outside its hours; headless Chromium 158.0.8127.18 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS, driven by page.mouse and the keyboard (Option+Tab in WebKit)
validated.finding: With the keys the grid was 1 tab stop, 2 Tabs took focus past it and an event on the fifth day took 7 key presses; as tab stops only it was 70 stops, 71 Tabs and 54 presses. Each key landed where the APG grid pattern says. Both engines.
validated.check: "scheduler: the grid is one tab stop: the second Tab after entering it is out of it", "scheduler: arrows move a slot or a day, Home and End the row, Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End the grid, Page Down and Page Up five slots", "scheduler: reaching Friday's Retro from before the grid takes few keys"; the negative control had no key handler and made every cell a tab stop

rules.rule: A control that reveals clamped text MUST show only while the text overflows its clamp (measured, and measured again when the width changes), and MUST be a toggle: one button that stays in place, keeps focus, carries aria-expanded and collapses the text again.
rules.why: Shown on text that fits, it is a tab stop that does nothing. Removed once pressed, it takes focus with it to the body and leaves no way to collapse.
rules.note: The APG disclosure pattern is the source for the toggle and aria-expanded only. Measure in a way that still holds while the text is open (its full height against the clamp's height), or the button hides itself once pressed.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a feed of 12 articles whose text is clamped to three lines; headless Chromium 158.0.8127.18 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS, driven by page.mouse and the keyboard (Option+Tab in WebKit)
validated.finding: The button showed on exactly the 7, 5 and 4 of 12 posts that overflowed at 320, 480 and 800px. Always shown, 7 of 12 buttons at 480px changed nothing when pressed. As a toggle it kept focus and returned the text to its clamped height on a second Enter; as a one-way control it removed itself and focus fell to the body. Both engines.
validated.check: "feed: See more shows exactly on the posts whose clamped text overflows, at 320, 480 and 800 wide" and "feed: every See more that shows changes how much text is shown when pressed" (control: always shown), "feed: See more is a toggle: it states its state, keeps focus when pressed, and the same button collapses the text" (control: expands and removes itself)

rules.rule: A virtualised list or feed MUST keep the item that holds focus in the DOM when it scrolls out of the rendered window, in its place in the order.
rules.why: Removing the focused node drops focus to the body: the list's keys stop working, and the user's place is gone with it.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a virtualised feed of 200 fixed-height articles in a 480px scroll box; headless Chromium 158.0.8127.18 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS, driven by page.mouse and the keyboard (Option+Tab in WebKit)
validated.finding: Scrolled 8000px away, the focused article was still mounted among 10 of 200 and Page Down moved on to the next article and brought it into view. Unmounted like the rest, focus was on the body and Page Down did nothing. Both engines.
validated.check: "feed, virtualised: the focused article stays mounted when scrolled far away, and Page Down goes on from it"; the negative control unmounted the focused article with the others

rules.rule: Roving focus SHOULD follow `focus()` with `scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest', inline: 'nearest' })`, so an item only partly visible inside a scrolling container is brought fully into view.
rules.why: `focus()` on an item partly visible in a scrolling container (a palette grid, a listbox) leaves it partly cut off.

validated.where: a palette grid in a scroll box with roving focus, and a listbox, web components, headless Chromium with the real keyboard
validated.finding: Moving focus to a cell half outside the grid's scroll view with focus() alone left the cell clipped; with the added scrollIntoView call it scrolled fully in
validated.check: the palette and listbox roving-focus tests; fail on the code before the change (negative control run by the build session, not re-run here)

rules.rule: Hover MUST change only a part's face (one step toward the text colour), never its box, MUST NOT look like the pressed state, and MUST NOT answer on a part that holds state (pressed, checked, selected, open, disabled).
rules.why: A hover that moves the box shifts targets under the pointer; a hover that looks pressed reads as a click; state that flickers on hover hides the state.

validated.where: a web-component library, Chromium (Playwright), every showcase part
validated.finding: Each interactive part's paint changes under a real pointer and its box does not; latched, checked and disabled parts do not change.
validated.check: browser test with negative controls: a key whose hover is the pressed fill fails

rules.note: How fast the change runs is paint, not behaviour: ui-materials gives the timing (in at once, out over the system's settle duration). The validation below proved the face and the box, not a duration.

rules.rule: Every hover rule MUST sit inside @media (hover: hover), so a touch screen never paints one.
rules.why: A tap leaves a sticky hover on touch screens, which then reads as state.

validated.where: a web-component library, Chromium (Playwright)
validated.finding: Under touch emulation (hover: none) no hover paint appears; a rule outside the media query is caught.
validated.check: browser test with CDP touch emulation (setEmulatedMedia does not emulate hover; touch emulation does)

rules.rule: In a menu or pop-up list the pointer MUST move the one active row the arrow keys move; persistent lists tint the row under the pointer instead.
rules.why: Two highlights (keyboard and pointer) in one pop-up make Enter's target ambiguous.

validated.where: a web-component library, Chromium (Playwright)
validated.finding: Moving the pointer over a select's and a menu's rows moves the active row and the focus.
validated.check: browser test

rules.rule: A secondary control revealed on hover (a close mark, a row action) MUST keep its room while hidden (opacity, not display), MUST also show on focus and on the current item, and MUST always show where there is no hover (@media (hover: none)).
rules.why: Toggling display moves the item's box under the pointer; a hover-only control is unreachable by keyboard and on touch.

validated.where: document tabs with close marks, Chromium (Playwright)
validated.finding: The mark is hidden on other tabs, shown on the chosen tab and under the pointer, and the tab's width does not change when it appears.
validated.check: browser test reads opacity and tab width at rest and under the pointer; fails on the old build

validated.where: a number field with a minus and a plus key revealed on hover and focus, web component, headless Chromium, a second browser context with touch and mobile emulation for the coarse pointer
validated.finding: At rest with a fine pointer the keys had opacity 0 and kept their room; in the touch context (pointer: coarse true) they had opacity 1. The component's query was (hover: none), (pointer: coarse); no check separated the two queries
validated.check: "the step keys show on a coarse pointer"; fails on the code before the change (negative control run by the build session, not re-run here)

rules.rule: Motion that is not the pointer's own movement (a thumb sliding to a choice, a cable settling, a flash) MUST be removed under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, and the part MUST be at its final place at once.
rules.why: Motion that follows an action can trigger vestibular disorders (WCAG 2.3.3); the state must not depend on it.

validated.where: a segmented tab strip whose thumb slides, and a canvas cord that swings after a node moves, web components, headless Chromium with reduced motion emulated
validated.finding: With motion the thumb's transition-duration was not 0s and it moved more than 10px to the chosen tab; under reduce the duration was 0s and the thumb covered the chosen tab (within 1.5px) at once. A cord's path differed one frame after a move and again after rest with motion, and was identical in all three readings under reduce
validated.check: "no transition under reduced motion" and the swing test's three readings; fails on the code before the change (negative control run by the build session, not re-run here)

rules.rule: Every target MUST take the pointer over at least 24px (WCAG 2.5.8, AA) at every size context, by its box, a transparent hit area, or a named exception (spacing, equivalent control, inline); the floor MUST be at least 24 CSS px, not only a rem value, and SHOULD rise to 44px under (pointer: coarse).
rules.why: A rem-only floor shrinks below 24px when a size context sets the root font size; 44px is the comfortable touch size (2.5.5).

validated.where: a web-component library, Chromium (Playwright)
validated.finding: A 1.5rem floor measured 18px with the small size context on the root; max(24px, 1.5rem) holds at every size.
validated.check: browser test asserts the token is 24px at sm, md and lg

rules.rule: A part smaller than the floor SHOULD take a transparent ::before, centred, at least the floor square, on a positioned part that does not clip its overflow; a dense grid whose pitch is below the floor cannot be fixed this way and needs spacing or larger parts.
rules.why: The hit area grows the target without moving any box; overlapping hit areas only hand each other's edges to the neighbour drawn later.

validated.where: a web-component library, Chromium (Playwright)
validated.finding: Thumbs, handles, a 2px playhead, close marks and tags take the pointer 11px from their centre at every size; routing points 33px apart overlap at 44px on touch.
validated.check: browser hit test (elementFromPoint through shadow roots) just inside the square's edge; fails with the hit area removed

rules.rule: A hit area for a slotted (light DOM) part MUST come from the part itself or its own stylesheet; ::slotted() selectors cannot give it a ::before.
rules.why: ::slotted() cannot be followed by a pseudo-element, so a container cannot grow the hit area of the content it slots.

rules.rule: Code that asks which element has focus MUST ask its own root (this.getRootNode().activeElement), never document.activeElement, whenever it can be rendered inside a shadow root; code that saves focus to restore later MUST save the deepest focused element (following shadowRoot.activeElement down from document.activeElement).
rules.why: From inside a shadow root, document.activeElement is the outermost host, so a menu rendered in another component's shadow tree finds no focused item and ignores Enter and the arrow keys.

validated.where: a menu component rendered inside a board's shadow root, Chromium (Playwright)
validated.finding: With document.activeElement, Enter on a focused menu item did nothing; reading the root node's activeElement fixed it.
validated.check: browser test passes with the fix and fails with the old lookup alone

validated.where: a menu button, a tree, a context menu and tabs rendered inside a host's shadow root, Chromium (Playwright)
validated.finding: With document.activeElement, arrows did nothing in the menu button and the tree and the context menu could not return focus; with the root's activeElement and the deepest focused element saved, all work. The tabs check also passed on the old build, so it proves nothing about that fix.
validated.check: browser test drives each inside a shadow host; three of its four checks fail on the old build

rules.rule: A custom element whose constructor sets attributes MUST NOT be created with document.createElement; create it from markup (innerHTML or a template), or move the attribute writes out of the constructor.
rules.why: The DOM refuses an element whose constructor gives it attributes (NotSupportedError: The result must not have attributes).

validated.where: a menu item custom element, Chromium (Playwright)
validated.finding: createElement threw NotSupportedError; building the items from escaped markup worked.
validated.check: page errors collected by the browser test

rules.rule: A listener on a host MUST find the part that was pressed from event.composedPath()[0], not event.target, which is retargeted to the host.
rules.why: event.target outside a shadow root is the host itself, so every press looks like a press on the whole component.

rules.rule: A component that shows one child at a time by setting the hidden attribute MUST also hide [hidden] children from its own stylesheet (::slotted([hidden]) { display: none !important }).
rules.why: hidden is only a user-agent style, so any author display rule on the child (display: grid on a slide) overrides it: every child stays shown and the component looks broken.

validated.where: a carousel web component with slides styled display: grid, Chromium (Playwright)
validated.finding: All slides stayed displayed and Next appeared to do nothing; with the slotted rule exactly one slide shows and Next moves it.
validated.check: browser test reads each slide's computed display; fails on the old build

rules.rule: A component that styles its light-DOM children through an adopted style sheet MUST adopt the sheet into the root it is in (`getRootNode()`) as well as the document.
rules.why: A sheet adopted on the document does not reach into a shadow root, so the component renders unstyled once it is placed inside another component's shadow root.

validated.where: an inspector web component that styles its light-DOM children by an adopted sheet, placed inside a host's shadow root, headless Chromium

rules.rule: Escape MUST close only the innermost open layer: a dialog or drawer MUST NOT close on the Escape that closes a menu, popover or tooltip open inside it.
rules.why: A native popover closes itself on Escape, and a dialog primitive that hears Escape on the document (ignoring defaultPrevented) closes too, so one key takes away both the menu and the work under it.

validated.where: a drawer, a dialog and an alert dialog on a headless dialog primitive in a React UI kit; found with real keys in headless Chrome, tested in vitest with happy-dom (the open popover stubbed)
validated.finding: With a menu open inside, Escape closed the drawer as well. Cancelling the dialog's close while :popover-open matches inside its panel keeps the drawer open; the next Escape closes it.
validated.check: unit test "Escape with a native popover open inside closes only that popover" fails on the code before the fix (re-run at the fix's parent commit with the new test) and passes after

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a record of three sections (text fields, a select, a date field with a picker popup, a field with a clear button, a field with steppers), an Edit button per section, Edit, Save and Cancel for the whole record and a New record button; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard
validated.finding: The rule holds between a popup and an editing scope that is not a dialog: with a native auto popover open inside a section in Edit, the keydown still reached the page, and a scope handler that did not check for an open popup cancelled the section, and dropped its draft, on the Escape that closed the popup. Checking for an open popup first, the first Escape closed only the popup and the second cancelled the section. Both engines, popup opened by pointer and from the keyboard.
validated.check: "escape: with the picker popup open, the first Escape closes the popup only and the second cancels the section" and "escape: the same with the popup opened from the keyboard"; the negative control let the scope's handler act on every Escape

rules.rule: A popup opened from inside a modal dialog MUST render inside that dialog, or in the top layer above it, never in a portal outside it.
rules.why: Everything outside a modal dialog is inert and drawn under the top layer, so a popup portalled to the body cannot be clicked or focused and opens underneath.

rules.rule: An auto popover opened from inside another MUST be nested in it: a DOM descendant, shown by an invoker inside it, or anchored to it.
rules.why: Only one auto popover shows at a time unless they are nested, so showing an unrelated one light-dismisses the popover it was opened from.

rules.rule: An overlay that has to appear above all other content on the page SHOULD be shown in the top layer: a dialog opened with showModal(), or a popover.
rules.why: The top layer is made by the browser to hold such elements and sits on top of every other layer of the document, so nothing else on the page can paint over what is in it.
rules.note: The source says what the top layer is and which elements enter it; it does not mention z-index.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: a sortable list of six rows in a page that scrolls, each dragged by a handle (mouse past 4px, finger after 250ms), with a keyboard mode on the handle and Move up and Move down buttons; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and page.keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only; the list in a frame with overflow: hidden and a transform, followed by a positioned panel with a z-index
validated.finding: A drag preview shown as a manual popover, carried out of the frame and over the panel, was painted there (screenshot pixel) and was top-most (hit test). The same preview as an absolutely positioned child of the frame was clipped: the pixel and the hit test both gave the panel. With no clipping ancestor the two behaved alike. Both engines.
validated.check: "preview: carried out of a clipping, transformed frame and over a later stacking context, the preview is painted and top-most"; negative control: an absolutely positioned preview inside the frame

rules.rule: While a modal dialog is open, the content outside it MUST be inert: users cannot interact with it, and Tab and Shift+Tab do not leave the dialog.
rules.why: A dialog is modal only if what is under it cannot be reached; showModal() makes every element outside the dialog inert, and a custom modal has to do the same.
rules.note: Neither source asks for the page scroll to be locked.

rules.rule: When a dialog holds enough content that focusing its first interactive element could scroll the start of the content out of view, the dialog SHOULD give a static element at its top (the title or first paragraph) tabindex="-1" and focus that on open.
rules.why: The first focusable element of a long dialog or drawer can be far down it, and focusing it opens the panel scrolled past its title.
rules.note: The APG calls this advisable; otherwise focus goes to the first focusable element.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a drawer of 60 paragraphs opened by showModal(), whose only tabbable element is a Close button at its end; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse
validated.finding: Focusing the first tabbable element, as a focus trap does, opened the drawer scrolled about 1,560px with its title about 1,525px above the viewport, and so did showModal() alone. With tabindex="-1" on the title and focus put there, it opened at 0 with the title in view and focus inside. Both engines. showModal() alone also chose the title once it had tabindex="-1".
validated.check: "overlay: a long drawer opens at its start, with its title in view and focus inside it"; the negative control focused the first tabbable element

rules.rule: A Move menu opened from a table cell MUST render outside the table's scroll box (fixed to the viewport or in the top layer).
rules.why: The scroll box clips its content and a cell that truncates text clips its own. A menu rendered in the cell is cut off or cannot be hit, worst for the last visible rows, whose menu has to extend past the box.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: an HTML table of 6 columns and 8 rows in a scroll box, with a sticky header row and a sticky first column, columns reordered by the header and rows by a handle; headless Chromium 159 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only
validated.finding: Every menu item was the element under its own centre point, including a row menu that extended below the scroll box's bottom edge. Both engines. Rendered in the cell, the items were not hit-testable.
validated.check: "col: the open Move menu is hit-testable past the scroll box and the cell" and "row: the open Move menu is hit-testable past the scroll box and the cell"; the negative control rendered the menu absolutely inside the trigger's cell

rules.rule: While a modal dialog is open the page behind it MUST NOT scroll: showModal() does not stop it, so the root element takes overflow: hidden until the dialog closes.
rules.why: A modal dialog makes the page inert but leaves it scrollable. A wheel, a swipe or a scroll key meant for the dialog moves the page under it, and the dialog closes on a different place from where it was opened.
rules.note: Not proven: keeping the scrollbar's room so nothing shifts sideways. With a root scrollbar styled to take 15px (::-webkit-scrollbar), scrollbar-gutter: stable on the root did not hold the room in either engine and the page shifted 15px; a native scrollbar that takes room could not be had headless.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a 4,000px page with a short dialog and a long drawer, both opened by showModal(); headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse (wheel) and the keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only
validated.finding: With showModal() alone the page scrolled 400px under a wheel over the backdrop and under a wheel over a dialog that does not scroll, scrolled 3,520px on PageDown, ArrowDown and End pressed inside the dialog, and scrolled 900px when the wheel went on past the end of the drawer. Both engines; a swipe on the backdrop scrolled it in Chromium. With overflow: hidden on the root none of these moved the page, the drawer still scrolled itself, and the page kept its scroll position on open and after close.
validated.check: "overlay: a wheel over the backdrop leaves the page where it was", "overlay: a wheel over a dialog that does not scroll leaves the page where it was", "overlay: PageDown, ArrowDown and End from inside the dialog leave the page where it was", "overlay: touch: a swipe on the backdrop leaves the page where it was" and "overlay: a long drawer scrolls itself, and at its end the wheel does not move the page" (negative control: no lock); "overlay: the page keeps its scroll position when the dialog opens and after it closes" (negative control: a lock by position: fixed on the body with no offset, which draws the page from its top)

rules.rule: A popup that previews a draft live MUST put back the last applied value on Escape and on Cancel.
rules.why: The preview has already changed what the page shows. If closing leaves it there, Cancel has applied the draft; if closing puts back the first value, it has undone an earlier Apply.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a colour popup whose slider previews on its trigger, with Apply and Cancel; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard
validated.finding: After five arrow presses on the slider, Escape and Cancel each put the trigger back to the applied hue, closed the popup and returned focus to the trigger. After an Apply and a second draft, Escape put back the applied hue, not the one the page loaded with. Both engines.
validated.check: "picker: Escape puts back the last applied colour", "picker: Cancel puts back the last applied colour" and "picker: after an Apply, Escape puts back the applied colour, not the first one"; the negative controls closed without restoring, and restored the value the page loaded with

rules.rule: A page that locks scroll with overflow: hidden on the root SHOULD set scrollbar-gutter: stable on the root from the start, so the room of a scrollbar that takes room stays when the lock removes the bar; padding the root by the scrollbar's width MAY be used but holds only content in flow.
rules.why: Where the scrollbar takes room, removing it widens the page by the bar's width: centred content jumps half of it and anything anchored to the right edge all of it, and jumps back when the dialog closes. A padding on the root does not move fixed or right-anchored absolute parts, which still jump. With overlay scrollbars the bar takes no room and neither is needed.

validated.where: a tall page with a centred column, a right-anchored and a fixed mark, headed Chromium 158 with classic 15px scrollbars (overlay scrollbars disabled by flag)
validated.finding: The plain lock moved the column 7.5px and both marks 15px. With scrollbar-gutter: stable on the root nothing moved. With padding-right of the bar's width the column held and both marks still moved 15px. WebKit could not be made to draw a classic scrollbar, so it was not measured there.
validated.check: drop the gutter declaration: the column moves 7.5px and the right-anchored marks 15px

rules.rule: A popup that closes on Escape MUST first put back an unsent typed edit in a field inside it, keep itself open and leave focus in that field, and MUST close on the next Escape; a field's own Escape handler MUST NOT be relied on, since a document-level capture handler hears the key first.
rules.why: A popup's dismiss handler sits on the document in the capture phase, so the field never hears Escape; the user loses the draft and the popup in one key.

validated.where: a popover colour picker with a printed number beside each slider, a web component set in shadow DOM, headless Chromium driven by the real keyboard
validated.finding: With a typed, unsent value in a slider's number, the first Escape put the number back to the value shown, left the colour and the popover as they were and kept focus in the number; the second Escape closed the popover. Before the fix the first Escape closed the popover and dropped the text. No change event fired either time.
validated.check: "Escape in a slider number with an unsent edit puts the edit back and keeps the picker open; the next Escape closes"; fails on the code before the change (negative control run by the build session, not re-run here)

rules.rule: A date field MUST accept a date typed as digits alone (eight, or six with a short year) in the locale's field order.
rules.why: With inputmode="numeric" a phone's keypad has no slash, dot or hyphen, so a field that needs separators cannot be filled there.

validated.where: a date field and a date range field in a React UI kit, vitest with happy-dom
validated.finding: Digits typed with no separator were not read before; after, "19112026" reads 19 November 2026 in en-GB, and "11192026" the same in en-US.
validated.check: unit test "reads eight digits, or six with a short year, typed with no separator, in the locale's order" fails on the code before the fix (re-run at the fix's parent commit with the new test) and passes after

rules.rule: A date field whose calendar grid is Gregorian MUST format and parse with the Gregorian calendar (calendar: 'gregory') in every locale.
rules.why: Thai formatting writes Buddhist-era years (2569) and Persian writes Jalali dates, so an edit stores a date centuries off and the grid's month names disagree with its days.

validated.where: a date field and a date range field in a React UI kit, vitest with happy-dom
validated.finding: th-TH wrote the year as 2569 and the round trip failed; with the Gregorian calendar forced it writes 19/11/2026 and reads it back.
validated.check: unit test "writes the Gregorian date in any locale, and reads back what it wrote, in the locale's own digits" fails on the code before the fix (re-run at the fix's parent commit with the new test) and passes after

rules.rule: A date field MUST read back every text its own formatter writes, including the locale's own digits (Arabic-Indic, Persian).
rules.why: A locale formatter writes non-Latin digits, so a parser that knows only ASCII cannot read the field's own value after an edit.

validated.where: a date field and a date range field in a React UI kit, vitest with happy-dom
validated.finding: ar-EG and fa-IR text failed the format-then-parse round trip before; mapping the locale's digits to ASCII first makes it pass in seven locales.
validated.check: unit test "writes the Gregorian date in any locale, and reads back what it wrote, in the locale's own digits" fails on the code before the fix (re-run at the fix's parent commit with the new test) and passes after

rules.rule: A typed four-digit year MUST be taken as written; a short-year pivot MAY apply only to a one- or two-digit year.
rules.why: Applying the pivot to every year turns 0005 into 2005, and a year written without four-digit padding cannot be read back.

validated.where: a date field and a date range field in a React UI kit, vitest with happy-dom
validated.finding: 12/11/0005 was read as 2005 before; after, it stays 0005 and is written back padded to four digits.
validated.check: unit test "takes a four-digit year as it is, and writes every year in four digits" fails on the code before the fix (re-run at the fix's parent commit with the new test) and passes after

rules.rule: A calendar MUST stop at the first and last dates it can represent (years 0001 and 9999): the days past them disabled and navigation stopping there.
rules.why: Stepping past year 9999 crashes or wraps, and an ISO string compare puts "10000-01-01" before "9999-12-31".

validated.where: a date field and a date range field in a React UI kit, vitest with happy-dom
validated.finding: Before the fix, paging past December 9999 failed; after it, the title stays December 9999 with the later days disabled, and January of year 1 likewise.
validated.check: unit test "shows December 9999 and January of year 1, with the days past them disabled and the keys stopping at them" fails on the code before the fix (re-run at the fix's parent commit with the new test) and passes after

rules.rule: A calendar's first day of the week MUST follow the locale even where the engine lacks Intl.Locale week info, by a fallback table of regions.
rules.why: Firefox has neither getWeekInfo() nor weekInfo, so a grid that relies on them starts every locale's week on the same default day.

validated.where: a date field and a date range field in a React UI kit, vitest with happy-dom
validated.finding: Without the engine's week info the grid started its week on a different day than with it; with the region table it starts on the same day.
validated.check: unit test "starts the week on the same day without the engine's week info" fails on the code before the fix (re-run at the fix's parent commit with the new test) and passes after

rules.rule: Text that is not a whole date MUST stay in the field as typed and marked aria-invalid, while the value the form holds is emptied.
rules.why: Replacing the text loses what the user typed; keeping the last good date leaves the field showing one thing while the form submits another.

validated.where: a date field and a date range field in a React UI kit, vitest with happy-dom
validated.finding: Before, unreadable text on blur left the form holding the previous date; after, the text stays, is invalid, and the hidden value is empty.
validated.check: unit test "text that is not a date stays as typed and is invalid, and the date is emptied: the form never holds a date the field does not show" fails on the code before the fix (re-run at the fix's parent commit with the new test) and passes after

rules.rule: Escape in a field MUST revert only an uncommitted draft, and with no draft MUST be left to propagate unhandled.
rules.why: Escape is the user's undo for a half-typed value, but a field that always takes Escape keeps a surrounding dialog from closing.

validated.where: a date field and a date range field in a React UI kit, vitest with happy-dom
validated.finding: Escape after typing put back nothing before; after, it restores the held date's text, and a second Escape is not default-prevented.
validated.check: unit test "Escape puts back the text of the date held; with nothing typed it is left to the page" fails on the code before the fix (re-run at the fix's parent commit with the new test) and passes after

validated.where: a number window that takes typed digits with Enter, and a scrubbed value that starts typing on a click, web components in shadow DOM, headless Chromium with the real keyboard
validated.finding: Digits typed and not sent are dropped by Escape: the held value and the printed number are unchanged. Not shown: a second Escape with no draft
validated.check: "Escape drops a typed draft" and "a click starts typing with the value selected" (then `9`, Escape, value unchanged); fails on the code before the change (negative control run by the build session, not re-run here)

rules.rule: A date field with a calendar popup SHOULD open it from the field on Alt+ArrowDown and close it on Alt+ArrowUp.
rules.why: Keyboard users otherwise Tab to a separate button to reach the calendar; Alt+ArrowDown is the key the combobox pattern names for opening a field's popup.

validated.where: a date field and a date range field in a React UI kit, vitest with happy-dom
validated.finding: Alt+ArrowDown did nothing before; after, it opens the calendar with focus on the field's date, and Alt+ArrowUp closes it.
validated.check: unit test "Alt+ArrowDown in the field opens the calendar on its date; Alt+ArrowUp closes it" fails on the code before the fix (re-run at the fix's parent commit with the new test) and passes after

rules.note: The APG combobox lists these keys as optional and opens without moving focus; a calendar popup takes focus, since its grid is where the keys act.

rules.rule: After the first pick of a range, the calendar SHOULD preview the range to the day under the pointer, or else the focused day, and take it only on the second pick.
rules.why: Without a preview the user cannot see what the second pick will select; taking the range on hover would commit a range nobody chose.

validated.where: a date field and a date range field in a React UI kit, vitest with happy-dom
validated.finding: No preview showed before; after, the hovered or focused day previews the range in the selected paint, a day before the start previews nothing, and the value changes only on the second pick.
validated.check: unit test "after the first pick, the day under the pointer or focus previews the range; the range is only taken on the second pick" fails on the code before the fix (re-run at the fix's parent commit with the new test) and passes after

rules.rule: A range with only an end set SHOULD show that end in the calendar as one selected day.
rules.why: A range drawn only when its start exists hides a value the form holds.

validated.where: a date field and a date range field in a React UI kit, vitest with happy-dom
validated.finding: An end alone showed nothing in the grid before; after, that day is selected.
validated.check: unit test "a range with only an end selects that day" fails on the code before the fix (re-run at the fix's parent commit with the new test) and passes after

rules.rule: A whole range pasted into either field of a range SHOULD fill both fields.
rules.why: People copy a range as one piece of text; putting all of it into the start field leaves an unreadable start and an empty end.

validated.where: a date field and a date range field in a React UI kit, vitest with happy-dom
validated.finding: Before, a pasted range did not fill both fields; after, it is split on a dash, tilde or word and fills both.
validated.check: unit test "a whole range pasted into either field fills both" fails on the code before the fix (re-run at the fix's parent commit with the new test) and passes after

rules.rule: An end before its start MUST stay as typed, with both fields marked invalid and described by the reason, and the form MUST hold no range while the ends are inverted; the reason SHOULD be announced.
rules.why: Swapping the ends silently changes what the user typed; marking the fields without a reason leaves a screen reader user with no way to fix it.

validated.where: a date field and a date range field in a React UI kit, vitest with happy-dom
validated.finding: Before, both fields were invalid but carried no reason; after, each is described by "The end date is before the start date." and it is announced; the ends are never swapped.
validated.check: unit test "an end before its start stays as typed: both fields invalid and described by the reason, which is announced; never swapped" fails on the code before the fix (re-run at the fix's parent commit with the new test) and passes after

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a date range of two text fields and a calendar popup, each end held as YYYY-MM-DD in a hidden input; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by the real keyboard and mouse
validated.finding: A start typed after its end stayed as typed (2026-11-20, 2026-11-15), both fields invalid and described by the reason, which was announced once, and the form held nothing for either end until the end was fixed. Stored as typed with no mark, the form held 2026-11-20 to 2026-11-15; swapped, the typed start appeared in the end field. Both engines.
validated.check: "range: a start typed after the end stays as typed, both fields invalid with the reason, and the form holds no inverted range"; the negative controls stored the inverted range unmarked, and swapped the ends silently

rules.rule: A date field that stands in for a native date input SHOULD hold its value as that input does: a yyyy-mm-dd string, whatever format the locale displays.
rules.why: The displayed date follows the locale of the browser while the value is always yyyy-mm-dd, so the value a form or script reads does not change with the locale.
rules.note: The source states this of the native input (its value is normalized to yyyy-mm-dd and differs from the displayed format); holding a custom field to the same form is by parity. It says nothing of time zones or of how to test.

rules.rule: A calendar grid of days SHOULD take the keys of the APG date picker: arrows move by a day or a week, Home and End go to the first and last day of the week, Page Up and Page Down change the month, and Shift with them the year, keeping the day number or else the last day of the month.
rules.why: These are the keys a keyboard user already knows from the grid pattern, and without the paging keys a distant date is reached one day at a time.
rules.note: From the keyboard table of the APG date picker dialog example, which also keeps one day of the grid in the Tab sequence, as the grid pattern specifies.

rules.rule: When a range's calendar takes its second pick, both fields MUST show the dates picked: text left in either field (unreadable or half-typed) and its invalid mark MUST be dropped.
rules.why: A field's text is state of its own beside the date held. If the calendar stores the range and leaves that text, the field shows one thing, still marked invalid, while the form submits another.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a date range of two text fields and a calendar popup, each end held as YYYY-MM-DD in a hidden input; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by the real keyboard and mouse
validated.finding: With "2026-13-45" left in the start field, picking 12 and 18 November showed and stored 2026-11-12 to 2026-11-18 with no invalid mark. When the pick left the field's text alone the start field still showed "2026-13-45", invalid, while the form held 2026-11-12. The same by keyboard with "2026-11-" left in the end field. Both engines.
validated.check: "range: mouse: after the calendar's second pick both fields show the range picked, over a draft left in a field" and "range: keyboard: after the calendar's second pick both fields show the range picked, over a draft left in a field"; the negative control stored the picked range and kept each field's text and mark

rules.rule: A date field MUST take its typed text as a date when focus leaves it or on Enter, and MUST NOT read, mark, store or announce it on each key.
rules.why: On the way to a whole date the text passes through others ("2026-11-2" before "2026-11-25"). Read on each key, a half-typed end falls before its start, so the range is marked invalid, emptied and announced mid-typing, and a field rewritten with the date read corrupts the next key. A field that takes text only on Enter shows one date and holds another once focus has left.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a date range of two text fields and a calendar popup, each end held as YYYY-MM-DD in a hidden input; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by the real keyboard and mouse
validated.finding: Typing an end of 2026-11-25 after a start of 2026-11-10: with the commit on blur or Enter nothing held, marked or said changed through ten keys, and Enter held the range. With a commit on each key the ninth key ("2026-11-2", read as 2 November) emptied the stored start, marked both fields and announced the reason; where the commit also rewrote the field the text ended as "2026-11-025" and no end was held. With a commit on Enter only, Tab left the field showing "2026-11-2" while the form held 2026-11-15. Both engines.
validated.check: "range: typing an end key by key changes nothing held, marks nothing and says nothing until Enter; then the range is held as typed" (negative controls: a commit on every input event, with and without rewriting the field) and "range: a field commits when focus leaves it, as it does on Enter" (negative control: a commit on Enter only)

rules.rule: A custom field that submits through a hidden input MUST restore its initial value, and drop typed text, on its form's reset event.
rules.why: A form reset restores native controls only; the component's own state and its visible text stay as they were, so the form and the field disagree.

validated.where: a date field and a date range field in a React UI kit, vitest with happy-dom
validated.finding: Reset left the typed text and the changed date before; after, the date and its text are those first rendered.
validated.check: unit test "a form's reset puts back the date it was first rendered with, and drops typed text" fails on the code before the fix (re-run at the fix's parent commit with the new test) and passes after; the range field's reset test fails the same way

rules.rule: Validation of a custom field MUST point at its visible, focusable control, not at the hidden input that carries the value.
rules.why: A hidden input cannot take focus or be validated, so required is never reported and an error summary's link leads nowhere.

validated.where: a date field and a date range field in a React UI kit, vitest with happy-dom
validated.finding: Before, required was not reported and the error link focused nothing; after, the hidden input names the visible field, which takes the error, the focus and the clearing edit.
validated.check: unit test "with the form validation: required is reported, the link focuses the field, an edit clears the error" fails on the code before the fix (re-run at the fix's parent commit with the new test) and passes after

rules.rule: Two inputs under one label (the ends of a range) MUST each have their own id, with the label naming their group and the hint and error describing both.
rules.why: A field context made for one input gives both the same id, so the label, the hint and the error attach to one end only.

validated.finding: Both ends shared one id before; after, each has its own id and name, the label names the group, and the hint and error describe both.
validated.check: unit test "in a form field, each field has its own id and name; the label names the group; hint and error describe both" fails on the code before the fix (re-run at the fix's parent commit with the new test) and passes after

rules.rule: A field that rewrites its own value while focused (normalising `.2` to `0.2` on Enter) SHOULD set the selection and scroll the field to show the caret after rewriting.
rules.why: After the rewrite the caret goes to the end, but a narrow field does not scroll to show it, so the end of the text and the caret are out of view.

validated.where: a 12rem colour field with a long value, web component, headless Chromium with the real keyboard

rules.rule: An example of a field's expected format SHOULD be help text tied to the field with `aria-describedby`, not placeholder text. Where it is placeholder text, the field's error message MUST repeat the example and be tied to the field, and the placeholder MUST take a colour that meets the contrast required of help text.
rules.why: A placeholder is shown only while the value is empty, so the example is gone while the person types and when they check what they typed; some engines' own placeholder colour is under 4.5:1.

validated.where: a single text field taking one format, a static page driven by real mouse and keyboard input in Chromium and WebKit (Playwright)
validated.finding: After one typed character the example can be read as help text and cannot as placeholder text. With a placeholder, an error message that repeats the example puts it back on screen and in the field's description while the value is corrected. An engine's own placeholder colour on a white field measured 2.35:1 in WebKit and 4.61:1 in Chromium; given the help text's colour it is 7.07:1 in both.
validated.check: browser test: type one character; send a wrong value and type on; read the placeholder's computed colour. The typing check fails with the example as a placeholder, and the two error checks fail with the repeat or the `aria-describedby` tie removed, in both engines

rules.note: The test shows the mechanics, not a person using the form, and reads the description from the DOM, not from a screen reader. No source names the error-repeat fallback, and it helps only after a first wrong attempt; WCAG's wording favours the help text wherever the label alone does not give the format.

rules.rule: A saved record SHOULD open in Review: no key or press on a field changes a shown or a saved value until Edit is entered for a scope that holds the field.
rules.why: A record that opens editable takes any key that lands in it. One stray key changes what is shown, and where Enter saves, two change what is stored.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a record of three sections (text fields, a select, a date field with a picker popup, a field with a clear button, a field with steppers), an Edit button per section, Edit, Save and Cancel for the whole record and a New record button; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard
validated.finding: In Review a click on a field, a letter key and Enter left the shown and the saved value as they were, and a letter on the select's Review control changed nothing. With the record opened in Edit, the letter changed the shown value, the letter and Enter changed the saved value, and one letter on the select changed its draft. Both engines.
validated.check: "review: a key typed into a field of a saved record changes nothing, shown or saved" and "review: a letter typed on the Role control of a saved record changes nothing"; the negative control opened the saved record in Edit

rules.rule: Edit MUST make editable only the scope that was opened, one section or the whole record, and Save MUST commit only that scope's draft: another open section keeps its draft and stays in Edit.
rules.why: A field that turns editable without being opened takes typing nobody meant, and a Save that reaches past its scope stores a draft whose owner has not yet chosen to save or cancel it.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a record of three sections (text fields, a select, a date field with a picker popup, a field with a clear button, a field with steppers), an Edit button per section, Edit, Save and Cancel for the whole record and a New record button; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard
validated.finding: With one section opened, typing into a field of another section changed nothing and that field stayed readonly. With two sections open, Save in one stored its draft only; the other stayed in Edit with its draft and its saved value unchanged. Both engines.
validated.check: "scope: Edit on one section makes only that section editable" and "scope: Save in one section leaves the draft of another open section uncommitted and open"; the negative controls made every section editable on any Edit, and committed and closed every open scope on any Save

rules.rule: A new record MUST start as a draft in Edit; its first Save stores it and settles it into Review, and Cancel or Escape before that Save MUST leave no record behind.
rules.why: A new record in Review is empty fields that take no typing until one more press. A record stored at creation survives its own Cancel as an empty record.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a record of three sections (text fields, a select, a date field with a picker popup, a field with a clear button, a field with steppers), an Edit button per section, Edit, Save and Cancel for the whole record and a New record button; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard
validated.finding: A new record took typing at once and nothing was stored until its first Save, after which every section was in Review and a stray key changed nothing. Cancel and Escape on the unsaved draft left the count of saved records as it was. Both engines.
validated.check: "new: a new record takes typing at once", "new: the first Save stores the record and settles it into Review" and "new: Cancel/Escape on a draft that was never saved leaves no record behind"; the negative controls started the new record in Review, left it in Edit after Save, and stored it when it was created

rules.rule: In Review a control that only acts on a field's value (clear, a picker trigger, steppers) MUST NOT be operable or focusable: it leaves the row until its scope is in Edit.
rules.why: Left working, it changes what a field shows while the record says nothing is being edited and nothing was saved. Left as a dead button, it is a Tab stop that does nothing.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a record of three sections (text fields, a select, a date field with a picker popup, a field with a clear button, a field with steppers), an Edit button per section, Edit, Save and Cancel for the whole record and a New record button; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard
validated.finding: In Review the record had 11 Tab stops and none was an acting control; presses where clear, a stepper and the picker trigger sit in Edit changed no shown value and opened no popup. With the controls left working, the record had 15 stops and three fields showed values that were not the saved ones while every section was in Review. Left as dead buttons they added 4 stops that did nothing. Both engines. The paint side (the controls leave the row) is ui-materials construction.md, States.
validated.check: "acting: in Review no acting control is a Tab stop", "acting: in Review a press where clear and a stepper sit changes no shown value" and "acting: in Review the picker popup cannot be opened and no day picked"; the negative controls kept the controls in the row, working, and kept them as focusable buttons that do nothing

rules.rule: Entering or leaving Edit MUST NOT move or resize a row, a section or a field's box: Review draws the value in the same box the field has in Edit.
rules.why: A Review value drawn as plain text is shorter than the field, so every row below moves when a scope opens or closes, and a pointer resting on the next control presses something else.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a record of three sections (text fields, a select, a date field with a picker popup, a field with a clear button, a field with steppers), an Edit button per section, Edit, Save and Cancel for the whole record and a New record button; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard
validated.finding: Nothing moved or resized (0px) when the whole record entered Edit, and a pointer resting on the next section's Edit button still pressed it after the section above was opened from the keyboard. With Review drawn as one line of text, 24px against the field's 36px, the last section moved 60px, the next section moved 36px and the resting pointer's press landed on the page background. Chromium and WebKit gave the same numbers.
validated.check: "size: no row, section or value box moves or resizes when the whole record enters Edit" and "size: a pointer resting on the next section's Edit still presses it after the section above enters Edit"; the negative control drew the Review value as plain text in place of the box

rules.rule: Escape MUST cancel one scope, the one that holds focus, or the last one opened when focus is in none: its draft is dropped, and any other open scope keeps its draft and stays in Edit.
rules.why: An Escape that cancels every open scope throws away a draft the user was not looking at; one that does nothing leaves the keyboard without a cancel. Focus is not always inside the scope: a popup closed by Escape can leave it on the body.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a record of three sections (text fields, a select, a date field with a picker popup, a field with a clear button, a field with steppers), an Edit button per section, Edit, Save and Cancel for the whole record and a New record button; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard
validated.finding: With two sections in Edit, Escape in a field of one cancelled that one and left the other open with its draft. After a picker popup opened by a pointer was closed with Escape, WebKit left focus on the body; a handler that acts only when focus is inside a scope then ignored the next Escape there, and the fall-back to the last scope opened cancelled it. Both engines for the first finding, WebKit for the second.
validated.check: "escape: cancels the section that holds focus and leaves another open section and its draft"; the negative controls cancelled every open scope, and swallowed Escape. The fall-back: "escape: with the picker popup open, the first Escape closes the popup only and the second cancels the section" under ?break=escape-needs-focus, which failed in WebKit and passed in Chromium

rules.rule: When a scope leaves Edit, focus MUST go to the button that opened it, found in the page as it is after the change; Save and Cancel leave with the scope, so without the move nothing visible holds focus.
rules.why: The Save and Cancel buttons are gone when the scope closes. Focus then sits on the body or on a hidden button, and if the Edit buttons were re-rendered, a remembered node is detached and focusing it does nothing.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a record of three sections (text fields, a select, a date field with a picker popup, a field with a clear button, a field with steppers), an Edit button per section, Edit, Save and Cancel for the whole record and a New record button; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard
validated.finding: After Save and Cancel pressed from the keyboard, Escape in a field, Enter in a field and a mouse Save, focus was on the Edit button that opened the scope. Without the move, Save and Cancel left focus on the body (Chromium) or on the hidden button (WebKit), 12 Tab presses or 1 Shift+Tab from the opener; Escape and Enter in a field left it on the field, which stays visible in Review. With the Edit buttons re-rendered on close, focusing the remembered node did nothing and the results were the same as with no move. Both engines.
validated.check: the five "focus: after ..." checks; the negative controls made no focus call, and re-rendered the Edit buttons so the remembered opener was detached

rules.rule: When the button that opens a scope leaves as the scope enters Edit, focus MUST move into the scope, to its first field.
rules.why: The pressed Edit button is replaced by Save and Cancel. Without a move, focus is on the body or on a hidden button and the next key goes nowhere.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a record of three sections (text fields, a select, a date field with a picker popup, a field with a clear button, a field with steppers), an Edit button per section, Edit, Save and Cancel for the whole record and a New record button; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard
validated.finding: After Enter on a section's Edit button, focus was on the section's first field and a typed digit landed in it. Without the move, focus was on the body (Chromium) or on the hidden Edit button (WebKit) and the digit was lost. Both engines.
validated.check: "focus: entering Edit puts focus on the first field of the scope"; the negative control made no focus move on entering Edit

rules.rule: A control that needs an API some engines lack (EyeDropper) MUST be offered only where the API exists (`EyeDropper in window`).
rules.why: Where the API is missing the control throws when pressed and does nothing the user can see.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a colour popup with a button that opens the screen colour picker; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse
validated.finding: WebKit has no EyeDropper: offered without detection, pressing the button threw a ReferenceError and nothing happened on the page; with detection the button is absent there. Chromium has the API, so the control cannot fail there: the proof is from one engine.
validated.check: "picker: no control is offered that the engine cannot run"; the negative control offered the button without detecting the API

rules.rule: Where a capability the interface offers cannot run in the current engine or context (an effect, an input method, a permission, an API), the interface MUST say so where the capability is offered: leave the control out (`support.detect-api`), disable it with its reason in visible text beside it or in its label, or label the fallback where it renders. It MUST NOT render a substitute that looks like the capability without saying so, and a `title` alone MUST NOT carry the reason. Where both fit, an option among several SHOULD be disabled with its reason, so the set is the same in every engine, and a lone action SHOULD be left out. A stored choice that cannot run SHOULD move to the fallback and say so.
rules.why: A silent fallback looks like a fault: the person chose the option, sees nothing change, and cannot tell a missing capability from a broken one. A `title` reaches only a pointing device (HTML Standard, the title attribute).

validated.where: a self-contained page: a material switch (native radios Flat, Frosted, Refract) whose Refract option falls back to Frosted where detection says the lens is off (an SVG filter in backdrop-filter, drawn only by Chromium); headless Chromium 156 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and the keyboard, each engine run with the lens forced off and on, and with a stored Refract choice
validated.finding: Where the lens is off, the option is disabled, its label names what it needs, and a note says what is shown; a click on it and ArrowDown from Frosted change nothing, and a stored Refract loads as Frosted with the note. Where it is on, neither label nor note, and Refract renders. Measured: WebKit draws no pixel of the lens (the pane is identical to the same face and blur without it), so there Refract and Frosted would render alike.
validated.check: "support: an option that cannot run says so where it is offered" (by mouse and by keyboard), "a stored choice that cannot run moves to the fallback and says so" and "no option renders a look-alike under its own name", in both engines; negative control: the option stays enabled and the page renders the fallback with no note, under Refract's name, and every one of these checks fails on it

rules.rule: Every interaction check MUST be run once against the code without the change and fail there; a check that passes on the old code proves nothing.
rules.why: Interaction tests often pass vacuously: the event never fired, the selector matched nothing, or the assertion read a value that never changes.

validated.where: hover, hit-area and kanban drag tests
validated.finding: Each new check failed against the previous build and passed after the change.
validated.check: rerun with the old component file swapped in

rules.rule: Drag, hover and touch MUST be tested with the browser's own input (page.mouse, CDP Input.dispatchTouchEvent with touch emulation), reading the result from the DOM, the hit test or the live region; synthetic dispatchEvent does not count.
rules.why: dispatchEvent skips hit testing, pointer capture, default actions and the click that follows pointerup, which is where drag bugs live.

validated.where: kanban drag tests, Chromium (Playwright)
validated.finding: CDP touch events produce pointer events of type touch, so the delay constraint and the swipe case are testable headless.
validated.check: browser test

rules.rule: A test of a queued live region MUST wait until the region says the expected text (with a timeout), not read it right after the action.
rules.why: Announcers queue messages and space them out so each is read; the region shows the previous message for a while.

validated.where: kanban drag tests, Chromium (Playwright)
validated.finding: Read 50ms after Escape, the region still held "picked up"; waiting for the text passed.
validated.check: browser test

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS on Pointer Events: a sortable list of six rows in a page that scrolls, each dragged by a handle (mouse past 4px, finger after 250ms), with a keyboard mode on the handle and Move up and Move down buttons; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and page.keyboard, touch by CDP touch events under touch emulation in Chromium only
validated.finding: With position announcements debounced by 300ms, the region read right after the last of four arrow keys still said "Snare picked up, position 2 of 6"; waiting for the text found "position 6 of 6". Both engines; the earlier validation was Chromium only.
validated.check: "testing: read right after the last key, the region holds the new position" (fails on the correct page) against "testing: waited for, the region holds the new position"

rules.rule: A pointer or selection behaviour MUST be tested in WebKit as well as Chromium, since the engines differ on selection, capture and focus during a drag.
rules.why: A drag test that only runs in Chromium can pass while Safari users see the bug.

validated.where: knob drag selection, Playwright
validated.finding: The old knob selected page text in WebKit and not in Chromium, so a Chromium-only test passed on the buggy build.
validated.check: the same test in both engines; the WebKit run fails on the old build

rules.rule: A browser test of a drag MUST move the pointer at least twice over the target before releasing it.
rules.why: Drag-over logic runs on a move over the target, and a single move does not trigger it in every browser, so the release lands on a target that was never entered.

rules.rule: A check of a date held as a calendar day (a yyyy-mm-dd value) MUST run under a time zone behind UTC that changes its clocks and under one ahead of UTC, on dates that include the days the clocks change; a run under UTC alone does not count.
rules.why: A date handled as an instant slips a day only where the zone's offset or a clock change reaches it. Under UTC every such slip is zero, so a suite run there passes on code that is wrong for most users.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a date field that holds yyyy-mm-dd, typed into and stepped by the arrow keys; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS, each under UTC, America/Los_Angeles and Pacific/Kiritimati set as the browser context's time zone
validated.finding: Three naive routines were each swapped in: new Date('yyyy-mm-dd') read back with local getters, new Date(y, m, d).toISOString().slice(0, 10), and a day step of 86,400,000 ms from local midnight. Under UTC all three passed every check. Under America/Los_Angeles the first failed (2026-03-08 was held as 2026-03-07) and the third failed (ArrowUp on 2026-11-01 stayed on 2026-11-01) while the second passed; under Pacific/Kiritimati only the second failed. Neither zone alone caught all three. Both engines.
validated.check: "date: a typed date is held as typed" and "date: ArrowUp and ArrowDown step one day across both clock changes", each under the three zones, and four "date matrix" claims on which zone catches which routine; the negative controls were the three naive routines

rules.rule: A pressed pointer move sent by raw CDP (Input.dispatchMouseEvent of type mouseMoved) MUST carry the pressed button, as buttons: 1 or button: 'left'.
rules.why: Without it the page's pointermove reports buttons 0, as if the button had been released. Drag code that reads buttons never drags, and the test fails on code that is right.

validated.where: a self-contained page that records pointermove.buttons during a press; headless Chromium 158 on macOS over CDP (the protocol is Chromium's; no other engine)
validated.finding: Six mouseMoved events after a mousePressed arrived as pointermove with buttons 0 when sent with neither field, and with buttons 1 when sent with buttons: 1 or with button: 'left' alone. page.mouse sets it by itself: buttons 1 in Chromium and WebKit.
validated.check: "testing: a pressed move sent by raw CDP reports the button to the page"; the negative control sent the same moves with neither field

rules.rule: A check of what a press does (focus, a focus ring, anything that listens for pointerdown or mousedown) MUST press with the browser's mouse, never with el.click().
rules.why: el.click() fires the click event alone: no pointerdown, no mousedown and no change of focus. A check that reads focus or a ring after it passes on any code.

validated.where: a self-contained page with a native button and a focusable custom button that log their events; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS driven by page.mouse and, for the naive method, el.click()
validated.finding: A real click on the custom button fired pointerdown, mousedown, focus, pointerup, mouseup and click and focused it; el.click() fired click only and focused nothing. The check "a pointer press paints no focus ring" failed on a page that draws its ring on :focus when driven by page.mouse, and passed on that same page when driven by el.click(). Both engines. Also measured: WebKit does not focus a native button on a real click and Chromium does; and a press on a part the keyboard had already focused leaves :focus-visible matching by either method, in both engines.
validated.check: "testing: \"a pointer press paints no focus ring\", asserted after a press" by both methods; the negative control drew the ring on :focus, and the naive method passed on it

rules.rule: That a popup is top-most MUST be proved by the browser's hit test at the centre of each of its items (elementFromPoint returns the item), not by its visibility, its box or its z-index.
rules.why: A popup painted under another layer is still displayed, still has a box and still reports a z-index. Only the hit test asks what the pointer would reach.

validated.where: a self-contained page with a three-item menu beside a positioned band; headless Chromium 158 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS
validated.finding: With the menu's second item under a band of higher z-index, the automation library's visibility test, the item's box, its computed visibility and opacity and its parent's z-index all passed, and elementFromPoint at the item's centre returned the band. Both engines.
validated.check: "testing: \"the popup is top-most\", asserted on each menu item" by both methods; the negative control painted the menu under the band, and the naive method passed on it

rules.rule: A check that every stage of an interaction is announced MUST record the live region with a MutationObserver started before the first input and compare the whole sequence of messages; the region's text read at the end does not count.
rules.why: The region holds one message at a time, so its text at the end shows only the last stage and passes when the stages between were never announced. Waiting for each expected text catches a missing message but cannot see one written twice, or an extra one.

validated.where: a key-reordered list with a queued announcer, headless Chromium and WebKit
validated.finding: For four due messages the observer recorded 4, the end read 1. With position changes unannounced the observer recorded 2 and the end read still passed; with each written twice the observer recorded 6 while the end read and a wait for each text both passed.
validated.check: drop the position messages, then write each twice: the observer check must fail on both, and the end read passes on both

rules.rule: A check that enters into a React-controlled field the value it already shows MUST clear the field first (or enter a different value between); a paste or a key that leaves the value as it was runs no onChange.
rules.why: React fires onChange only when the field's value differs from the one it last saw. The browser still fires its input event, so the test's input is real and the handler under test is silently never called: a second paste of the same text proves nothing about the parser.

validated.where: a controlled React 18.3.1 input with a parser in onChange, beside a plain input with a native listener, headless Chromium and WebKit
validated.finding: A real paste of the value already shown fired 1 native input event and 0 onChange calls; after a clear it fired 1 onChange. The plain input's listener ran on the unchanged paste. Typing the one character already shown behaved the same way.
validated.check: paste the same value twice without clearing: the handler must not run the second time on the React field, and must run on the plain field

rules.rule: A component whose output depends on the current time (today's mark, a now-line, what is upcoming or overdue) MUST take that time as an input and MUST NOT read the clock itself; its checks pass the time in.
rules.why: A check of a clock-reading component is green only at the moment it was written for: it turns red at midnight and on every other day, or has to compute its expectations from the same clock and so proves nothing.

validated.where: a self-contained page, vanilla JS: a week time grid of 7 days by 10 hourly slots with six events in it and four outside its hours, the time passed in by the address and the browser's clock fixed by Playwright's page.clock in America/Los_Angeles; headless Chromium 158.0.8127.18 and WebKit 27.2 on macOS, driven by page.mouse and the keyboard (Option+Tab in WebKit)
validated.finding: The same assertions for one injected time were green at five wall clocks; with the component reading the clock they were green at one and red at four, and two renders four seconds apart, either side of midnight, disagreed on today. Both engines. The two clock-change days added nothing beyond being other days.
validated.check: "scheduler: today, the now-line and Upcoming follow the injected now at five wall clocks" and "scheduler: two renders four seconds apart, either side of midnight, agree on today"; the negative control read new Date() inside the component. "scheduler: the assertions for Wednesday 10:30 hold with that now injected and fail with another" shows the assertions do read the time

rules.rule: A check of coarse-pointer or no-hover styling MUST run in a context created with hasTouch and isMobile, MUST first assert `matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)').matches`, and SHOULD read the same property in a default context to show it differs.
rules.why: Without the guard a check can pass for the wrong reason, in a context where the query never matched.

validated.where: a web component page in headless Chromium, a second context with touch and mobile emulation
validated.finding: In the touch context matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)').matches was true and a hover-revealed key read opacity 1; in the default context the same key read opacity 0. Not tested: that the default context does not match, or that toggling touch emulation on a default page would not
validated.check: the guard and the two readings; fails on the code before the change (negative control run by the build session, not re-run here)

rules.note: Validated in one engine only (Chromium); testing rules aim for both. A WebKit run of the guard and the two readings would complete it.
